design.name: PathSpec-AR: exact chunk-autoregressive speculative sampling on the sampler-path space (Fast drafts coupled per position, plus optional context-speculative lookahead)
design.summary:
Main finding: an exact sampler exists, but with Fast as the draft it cannot be faster than running the target. The only exact speed-ups come from running the target itself in parallel.

1. Where exactness can be defined. Neither Fast nor Base has a tractable density over a chunk, so exactness can only be stated on the sampler-path space: each chunk together with its 4-node x0-renoise path. The target is therefore a chunk-AR kernel process, not the Base-70 clip. The default target, T_H, is exactly what `--specstep 1 --spec-nodes 0,1,2 --policy never` samples:
   - Base CFG-5 RePaint kernels at nodes 0, 1 and 2;
   - Fast's deterministic finish at node 3;
   - chunk 0 is plain Fast.
   A variant, T_H0, makes node 0 independent of the prefix; that change is below bf16 resolution. T_B adds a Base finish at node 3 and a Base chunk 0.
2. The algorithm. At every stochastic (chunk, node) transition, compute Fast's and Base's kernel means at the current exact state and couple the two Gaussians with the reflection maximal coupling (Algorithm 4 of De Bortoli et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.05370).
   - The coupling is done per latent position when the goal is to reuse the draft.
   - It is done on the whole state wherever lookahead is attempted.
   - The lookahead window (their Algorithm 3) and context speculation are exact add-ons.
3. The proof is per-transition exactness plus Markov induction. It holds under 8 stated assumptions (A1–A8).
4. Hard limit, from our own logs (legacy `--policy spec` runs, same target kernel):
   - The whole-chunk mean discrepancy is ||Δ|| = 37–148 at nodes 1–2, so the chance of accepting the whole state is at most about 1e-75.
   - Any exact scheme that reuses a Base evaluation made at a Fast-drafted state gains essentially no lookahead.
   - Expected speed-up is 0.93–1.0x versus the target run alone, which the logs put at about 750 s per clip.
   - The cause is structural. Distilled Fast's x0 looks like a sample, while undistilled Base's x0 is a posterior mean, so the two path measures barely overlap even if the video marginals matched.
   - For lookahead to pay off, Fast's x0 would have to be within 1.7% (node 1) and 0.6% (node 2) relative L2 of Base's RePaint x0. It is at 39–47% and 31–33%.
5. What Fast still contributes. Per-position coupling keeps an estimated 59–96% of Fast's sampled positions at no extra Base cost. That gives common random numbers with the Fast-only rollout, plus a free exact per-position TV map that can serve as the target-likelihood proxy for item 5.
6. Exact acceleration that does exist (UNVERIFIED estimates):
   - Parallelise the target itself: CFG branches on two GPUs, plus node-0 calls off the critical path under T_H0. This gives about 2.5–2.9x, roughly 260–300 s, on GPUs 4–7.
   - Context speculation: Fast proposes the not-yet-final previous chunk, and Base with that stale context is the draft. It can have high acceptance exactly where RePaint ignores the prefix. It pays off only with 6–8 GPUs and a node-1 acceptance that has not been measured.
7. Recommendation.
   - Report item 3 as "exact w.r.t. T_H; no speed-up is possible with Fast drafts, shown by a bound and by measured numbers."
   - Keep plan→render (114–206 s) as the practical method, judged with the item-4 batch protocol.
   - Before any exactness claim, fix the audit issues: seeded ξ/u streams, no `--resident`, `--policy never` asserted, stale docs.
   - The specstep runs have not produced output yet. jar s1234 hit CUDA out-of-memory at 04:41 CDT because another process held 57 GB on the same GPU.
design.target_definition:
NOTATION
- Chunks c = 0..12 (N = 13). Each chunk has 3 latent frames: d = 16x3x58x106 = 295,104 dimensions, i.e. P = 18,444 positions of 16 channels.
- Node sigmas s_0..s_3 = 0.99980 / 0.93727 / 0.83306 / 0.62469. These are indices 0/250/500/750 of binding_v2's shift-5 grid. Base receives t = 1000·s as a float; Fast receives the integer timesteps 999/937/833/625.
- X_<c = the committed clean latents of chunks 0..c-1 (3c latent frames).

T_H: the default target, and exactly what spec_v0 --specstep samples once ξ and u are seeded
- Chunk 0 is drawn from Fast's 4-node sampler P_F. spec_v0 skips chunk 0 because a.start = 1 and outs is empty.
- For each chunk c ≥ 1, given X_<c:
  - Draw z_0 ~ N(0, I_d).
  - For k = 0, 1, 2:
    - Draw ξ_k ~ N(0, I) over the prefix latents.
    - Compute m_k = x0 of Base-A14B on the window [(1-s_k)·X_<c + s_k·ξ_k ; z_k] at t = 1000·s_k, keeping the chunk slots only.
      - CFG 5. The conditional branch uses the empty camera_WM prompt, the start image in y/mask, and camera poses for frames 0..F-1 with F = 4(3c+2)+1. The unconditional branch uses Wan's default negative prompt.
      - Expert: high if t ≥ 947, low otherwise. So node 0 uses the high expert and nodes 1–2 the low expert.
    - Draw z_{k+1} ~ N((1-s_{k+1})·m_k, s_{k+1}^2 I).
  - X_c = x0_Fast(z_3; t = 625; Fast KV = sink 6 + window 18 latent frames holding exactly X_<c; y_c). This is deterministic and is committed by a clean t = 0 pass.
- The transition kernel is K_k(dz' | z, X_<c) = E_ξ N(z'; (1-s')·m_k(z, X_<c, ξ), s'^2 I), a Gaussian mixture over ξ.
- The path law is P_T = P_F(X_0) · Π_{c≥1} ∫ N(z_0) Π_k K_k(z_{k+1} | z_k, X_<c) · δ(X_c − x0_F(z_3; X_<c)).

T_H0: recommended
Same as T_H, but node 0's prefix input is ξ_0 alone, so node 0 no longer depends on the prefix.
- In T_H the prefix enters node 0 with weight 1-s_0 = 2.0e-4, about 1.5e-4 per entry (latent RMS ≈ 0.73).
- base_flow casts the window to bf16, where the half-ulp of ξ entries in [0.5, 1) is about 2e-3, so this signal is an order of magnitude below rounding.
- This is an explicit, documented change of target. It makes every chunk's node-0 call computable in advance with no verification.

T_B
T_H with Base also finishing: X_c = x0_Base(z_3) at s_3 (RePaint window), and chunk 0 through an L = 0 window. This needs a new branch, because torch.cat of an empty `outs` fails.
- Fast then has no influence on the output law.
- Not recommended: Base's x0 at σ = 0.625 is a posterior mean (blurry), and it adds a 4th Base call per chunk.

T_B^K
Base-only chunk AR with K stochastic steps per chunk. The 'always16' ceiling (3472–3556 s) is the deterministic-UniPC relative of this. It shows seams and ignores the camera (NIGHT3_NOTES.md:148, 160).

T*: the reference, which no chunk-AR kernel reaches
The Base-70 whole-clip law (UniPC, shift 10, CFG 5, 161 frames): 2834 s on one GPU, measured on jar s11. The task text says ~600 s; that figure does not match our single-GPU measurement.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT PRESERVED

| Property | Exact under PathSpec-AR? |
|---|---|
| Joint law of the 13 committed chunks under the chosen target (T_H / T_H0 / T_B) | YES |
| Law of any functional of the video (drift indicator, DINO-to-Base, flicker, boundary jump) equals its law under a target-only rollout | YES (equality in law, not pathwise) |
| Base-70 whole-clip marginal T* | NO. T* is a bidirectional 161-frame joint; T_H is a product of chunk kernels. |
| Base's true conditionals p_B70(X_c \| X_<c) | NO. Same-σ RePaint is a heuristic conditional. Prefix SNR (1-s)/s is 0.0002 / 0.067 / 0.20 at nodes 0/1/2, so the layout is drawn almost unconditionally, which is the known snap-back / camera-ignored failure (NIGHT3:136, 148, 160). |
| A Base-only 4-node sampler | NO under T_H/T_H0: node 3 and chunk 0 are Fast. YES under T_B. |
| Fast's own law | NO. At nodes 0–2 Fast only affects which realisation you get (reuse), not the law. |
| A model likelihood | NO. CFG-5 and x0-renoise define a sampler, not a density of Base. |

Only asymptotically exact SMC conditional samplers target p_B70(X_c | X_<c) itself:
- TDS, Wu et al., NeurIPS 2023: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.17775
- SMCDiff, Trippe et al.: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.04119 (not re-fetched; UNVERIFIED)

Their cost is particles × Base forwards, far above Base-70.
design.algorithm_pseudocode:
RNG (fixes audit bug MEDIUM-1)
- G(seed, c, k, stream) is a dedicated torch.Generator for each (chunk, node, stream).
- Streams: 'z0' (CPU; keeps common random numbers with Fast-only), 'eps' (CPU, as now via g), 'u' (dev0), 'xi' (dev1).

def base_mean(c, k, z, Xpre, xi, target):   # 1 Base CFG-5 call = 2 forwards (cond + uncond)
    pref = xi if (target == 'H0' and k == 0) else (1 - s[k]) * Xpre + s[k] * xi
    x0 = BaseA14B(cat(pref, z), t = 1000*s[k], expert = 'high' if 1000*s[k] >= 947 else 'low',
                  y = start image, poses 0..F-1, cfg = 5)[:, L:L+3]
    return (1 - s[k+1]) * x0

def fast_mean(c, k, z):                      # Fast KV holds exactly X_<c
    return (1 - s[k+1]) * FastX0(z, node k, chunk c)

def couple_pos(muD, muT, sg, eps, u):        # exact; maximal reuse of the draft
    zt = muD + sg*eps
    logr = -(|zt-muT|^2 - |zt-muD|^2).sum(channels) / (2 sg^2)   # shape [3,58,106]
    acc = log(u) <= min(0, logr)                                 # one u per position
    e = (muD-muT) / |muD-muT|_channels                           # e = 0 where muD == muT
    y = muT + sg*(eps - 2*(e·eps)*e)                             # reflection per position
    return where(acc, zt, y), acc

def couple_whole(muD, muT, sg, eps, u):      # exact; maximal P(output == draft), i.e. maximal lookahead
    zt = muD + sg*eps
    logr = -(||zt-muT||^2 - ||zt-muD||^2) / (2 sg^2)             # scalar over the chunk
    if log(u) <= min(0, logr): return zt, True
    e = (muD-muT) / ||muD-muT||
    return muT + sg*(eps - 2*(e·eps)*e), False

# ---------- A. SPEC-AR (γ = 1). The default; this is --specstep after the fixes ----------
def SPEC_AR(seed, target = 'H0'):
    X = [chunk0(target)]             # H/H0: Fast 4-node sampler; B: Base kernel with an L=0 window
    commit(X[0])
    for c in 1..12:
        z = randn(G(seed,c,0,'z0'))
        for k in 0,1,2:
            xi  = randn(G(seed,c,k,'xi'))
            muT = base_mean(c, k, z, cat(X), xi, target)     # GPU B (runs concurrently with muD)
            muD = fast_mean(c, k, z)                         # GPU F
            z, acc = couple_pos(muD, muT, s[k+1], randn(G(seed,c,k,'eps')), rand(G(seed,c,k,'u')))
            log(acc_pos = acc.mean(),
                dnorm = ||muD-muT|| / s[k+1],
                log10_whole_acc = log10(2*Phi(-dnorm/2)),
                resid_mean / resid_var of r = (z-muT)/s[k+1],
                mean(e·r))
        Xc = FastX0(z, node 3, chunk c) if target != 'B' else (1-0)*base_mean_x0(c, 3, z, cat(X))
        commit(Xc)
        X.append(Xc)
    return VAEdecode(cat(X))
# The null arm for testing (--specstep 2, 'target-only'): the same loop with
#   z = muT + s[k+1]*randn(G(seed,c,k,'eps'))   and no Fast call at nodes 0-2.

# ---------- B. PathSpec-AR-γ (De Bortoli Alg. 3 lifted to the (chunk, node) sequence) ----------
def PATHSPEC_AR(seed, gamma, verifiers):
    st = (c=1, k=0, z=z0(1), X=committed)
    while st.c <= 12:
        path = []
        cur = st
        for j in range(gamma):                              # 1) sequential Fast drafting, optimistic Fast commits
            muD = fast_mean(cur.c, cur.k, cur.z)
            eps = randn(...)
            xi  = randn(...)
            zn  = muD + s'*eps
            path.append((cur, muD, eps, xi))
            cur = advance(cur, zn)                          # when k == 2: X~_c = FastX0(zn, 3), commit to Fast KV, next chunk
        muTs = parallel_map(verifiers, base_mean, path)     # 2) one Base call per GPU; batching fails in the camera path
        for j, (cur, muD, eps, xi) in enumerate(path):      # 3) accept in order
            z, ok = couple_whole(muD, muTs[j], s', eps, rand(...))
            st = advance_exact(cur, z)                      # at k == 2: X_c = FastX0(z, 3) on the TRUE prefix
            if not ok:
                break
        rollback Fast KV to exactly st.X                    # A5; discard every drafted state after the first rejection
# With the measured whole-state ||Δ|| >= 37 this always breaks at j = 0, i.e. it becomes SPEC_AR with the worse (whole) coupling.
# It is kept only as the formal frame-level algorithm. Use gamma = 1 plus couple_pos in practice.

# ---------- C. CS-AR: context-speculative lookahead (target T_H0). The only exact lookahead that can be accepted ----------
# Idea: Fast proposes the previous chunk's CONTEXT (where Base-RePaint is insensitive), not the chunk's content (TV ~ 1).
# Lag-1 diagonal schedule: at tick τ the GPUs run
#     node 2 of chunk c | node 1 of chunk c+1 (speculative) | node 0 of chunk c+2 (context-free) | verify node 1 of chunk c+1
for each chunk c+1 once z_1^{c+1} exists (node 0 is context-free, precomputed):
    Xhat_c = FastX0(z_2^c, node 2, chunk c)                  # context proposal, available one node before X_c
    xi1  = randn(G(seed,c+1,1,'xi'))
    muS  = base_mean(c+1, 1, z_1, cat(X_<c, Xhat_c), xi1)    # stale-context Base = the DRAFT kernel
    muD  = fast_mean(c+1, 1, z_1)                            # optional: Fast content, for per-position reuse
    zs, _ = couple_pos(muD, muS, s2, eps1, u1a)              # exact sample of N(muS, s2^2 I)
    launch node 2 of chunk c+1 at zs (speculative; its context X_<=c will be final)
    when X_c = FastX0(z_3^c, 3) is final:
        muT = base_mean(c+1, 1, z_1, cat(X_<=c), xi1)        # verification with the SAME xi1
        z_2, ok = couple_whole(muS, muT, s2, (zs - muS)/s2, u1b)   # Lemma 3: exact w.r.t. the true kernel
        if ok: keep the speculative node-2 result
        else:  recompute node 2 at z_2 (costs one extra tick)
# Node 2 is never context-speculated: its predicted ||Δ_ctx|| is >> 1.35 (see acceptance_analysis).
design.unbiasedness_proof:
SETTING
- Transitions are indexed t = (c, k), for c = 1..12 and k = 0, 1, 2, in lexicographic order.
- The state before t is S_t = (X_<c, z_k^c).
- The target kernel is K_t(dz' | S_t) = ∫ N(z'; μT_t(S_t, ξ), s'^2 I) N(dξ), with s' = s_{k+1}.
- F = the deterministic finish at node 3 (Fast, or Base under T_B) plus the commit.
- The target path law is P_0 ⊗ Π_t [N(z_0) · K_t] pushed through F.

ASSUMPTIONS (each one is needed; the implementation hazards are named with it)
- A1. Equal isotropic Gaussians. Given (S_t, ξ_t), the draft kernel is N(μD_t, s'^2 I) with the SAME s' as the target. This holds because both use x0-renoise with fresh noise on the shared grid. It would fail if either side used a deterministic or ODE step, or a different sigma. De Bortoli et al. state that the method does not apply directly to deterministic samplers (https://arxiv.org/html/2501.05370v2).
- A2. No peeking. μT_t is a function of (S_t, ξ_t) only. μD_t (or a stale-context mean μS_t) may depend on the whole history, on ξ_t and on independent extra randomness, but not on the current (ε_t, u_t). Fast's KV cache and the stale context Xhat are functions of the history, so this holds.
- A3. Fresh randomness. ξ_t ~ N(0, I), ε_t ~ N(0, I_d) and u_t ~ U(0, 1) (per position, or one per chunk for the whole coupling) are mutually independent and independent of (history, S_t). Consequences:
  - They must come from dedicated generators.
  - They must never be reused from a draw that influenced S_t.
  - Reusing an ε that was drawn during drafting is fine, because it was drawn independently of S_t.
  - The current code draws ξ and u from unseeded global CUDA generators. Each run is still marginally exact, but the 8-seed batches are not i.i.d. (the audit's MEDIUM-1 bug).
- A4. Reuse only on equality. A target mean computed at a drafted state z~ (or with drafted context) is used only if the realised state is bitwise equal to z~, and the context used is the true X_<c with the same ξ.
- A5. Identical deterministic maps. F (node-3 finish, commit pass, sink/window eviction, and KV rollback under lookahead) is the same function in the speculative and the target-only samplers. In particular:
  - Fast's KV cache holds exactly X_<c when F is applied.
  - The node-0–2 Fast forwards leave no state behind. Each call rewrites the chunk slot at current_start (binding_v2 _kwargs), so this holds; it can be checked cheaply by comparing x0_F(z_3) with and without the preceding forwards.
- A6. Chunk 0 has the same law in both samplers.
- A7. Numerics. μT and μD are computed once (bf16 forward, fp32 x0) and the same tensors are used for the ratio and for the reflection. Exactness is with respect to the as-computed kernel; GPU nondeterminism perturbs μT at bf16 noise level. The ratio must be taken in fp32 (it is, at spec_v0:481).
- A8. Adaptive choices. The window γ, the coupling type (per position or whole), whether to speculate, and which Xhat to use may depend on the history, but not on the current (ε_t, u_t).

LEMMA 1 (whole-state reflection maximal coupling)
De Bortoli et al., Prop. 3.1 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.05370), after Bou-Rabee et al. 2020.
- Let Y~ = μD + s'Z and U ~ U(0, 1).
- Output Y~ if U ≤ q(Y~)/p(Y~); otherwise output μT + s'(I − 2ee^T)Z, with e = (μD − μT)/||μD − μT||.
- Then Y ~ N(μT, s'^2 I), and P(Y = Y~) = 2Φ(−||Δ||/2) = 1 − TV, with Δ = (μD − μT)/s'. This is the maximum over all couplings.
- Sketch: the accepted part has density min(p, q). The reflection across the bisecting hyperplane maps p to q, and the rejected mass (p − q)^+ onto (q − p)^+.

LEMMA 2 (per-position coupling)
- N(μ, s'^2 I_d) = ⊗_p N(μ_p, s'^2 I_16) for any partition of the coordinates.
- Apply Lemma 1 to each position p with independent (Z_p, U_p). The outputs are independent across positions with law N(μT_p, s'^2 I_16), so their product is exactly N(μT, s'^2 I_d).
- The per-position acceptance is 1 − TV_p.
- The event "every position accepted" has probability Π_p (1 − TV_p), which is at most 1 − TV_whole. So this coupling maximises reuse, not lookahead.

LEMMA 3 (composition, used by CS-AR)
- Suppose Y~ is an exact sample of N(μS, s'^2 I), built from randomness (Z', U') that is independent of (μS, μT) given S_t. Then Z := (Y~ − μS)/s' ~ N(0, I) is independent of (μS, μT).
- So Lemma 1 with draft N(μS, s'^2 I) outputs exactly N(μT, s'^2 I).
- Independence holds because μT depends on X_c, and X_c depends only on chunk c's own randomness, never on (Z', U').

THEOREM
For every t, conditional on the full history up to S_t (including discarded speculation), the law of the next state is K_t(· | S_t).
- Condition additionally on ξ_t, which is legitimate by A3.
- By A2 the draft mean is fixed. By A3, (ε_t, u_t) are fresh. By A4, any precomputed target mean equals μT_t at the realised state.
- Lemma 1, 2 or 3 then gives N(μT_t(S_t, ξ_t), s'^2 I). Integrating over ξ_t gives K_t.
- By A8, adaptivity does not matter: each transition's conditional law is K_t whatever coupling or window was chosen.
- By induction over t (the Ionescu-Tulcea / chain rule for Markov kernels), the joint law of all (z_k^c) equals the target path law.
- By A5–A6, X = F(path) has the target's law.
- Discarded lookahead does not matter: its values are never used once a rejection has occurred (A4), and the next transitions use fresh randomness.

COROLLARIES
- C1 (null test for item 4). For any functional f of the video, E_spec[f] = E_target-only[f]. The spec and target-only batches must show equal drift rates. This is a correctness check, not a quality claim.
  - A far stronger check per run: the residuals r_t = (z_{k+1} − μT_t)/s' must be exactly N(0, I_d). Over 36 transitions × 295k coordinates, a transition's mean should be 0 ± 0.0003 and its variance 1 ± 0.0005, and ⟨e, r⟩ ~ N(0, 1).
- C2 (what breaks exactness):
  - the legacy --policy spec, which redraws from p_T instead of the residual and applies a τ threshold at the last node;
  - temperature τ ≠ 1 (De Bortoli Prop. F.1: acts as guidance toward the draft);
  - an SDVG-style threshold;
  - Base regeneration on rejection;
  - --specstep under the sem/always/every/verify/sched policies;
  - claims about node 3 or chunk 0 under T_H.
  - --hint-lora or --plan-video combined with specstep leaves the law equal to K_T's, so the plan survives only through node 3. Specstep plus hints is therefore NOT an exact plan→render.
- C3 (not implied). The theorem says nothing about Base-70: Π_c K^RePaint ≠ p_B70.
design.acceptance_analysis:
DATA
Legacy `--policy spec` runs use the same target kernel (Base RePaint, CFG 5, full prefix) at nodes 1 and 2:
- specwm_out/spec_v0/sand_filling_up_jar/{spec_n12, spec_n123_tau0.5}_s{1234,4321,9999}: 72 (chunk, node) records;
- specwm_out/spec_v0/sandcastle_wave_impact/…: 48 records.

They log per-token acceptance and E[log r]. A token is 2x2 positions x 16 channels = 64 dims, 4,611 tokens per chunk (tok = 4 resolves to 2x2 on the 58x106 grid). Since E[log r]_token = −|Δ_tok|²/2, the whole-chunk discrepancy is ||Δ||² = −2 · 4611 · E[log r]. The per-position estimate assumes an even spread; by convexity it is a lower bound.

| Prompt | Transition σ→σ' | Per-token acc ↑ (logged) | E[log r]/token | Whole-chunk ‖Δ‖ ↓ | Whole-state acc ↑ | Per-position acc ↑ (est., lower bound) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| jar | 0.937→0.833 | **0.81** | −0.148 | **36.9** | **≈1e-75** | **≥0.89** |
| castle | 0.937→0.833 | <u>0.67</u> | −0.438 | <u>63.5</u> | <u>≈1e-221</u> | <u>≥0.82</u> |
| jar | 0.833→0.625 | 0.60 | −0.641 | 76.9 | <1e-300 | ≥0.78 |
| castle | 0.833→0.625 | 0.33 | −2.383 | 148.2 | <1e-300 | ≥0.59 |
| both (est.) | 0.9998→0.937 | not logged | – | ≈12–36 | ≤1e-9 | ≈0.90–0.96 |

The node-0 row is an estimate: the scale factor (1−s')/s' is 0.067 there versus 0.200 at node 1, and the x0 gap is assumed to be 1.0–1.7x node 1's. UNVERIFIED; the first specstep run logs it as spec_dmean_0.

WHAT LOOKAHEAD WOULD NEED
- Whole-state acceptance ≥ 0.5 needs ||Δ|| ≤ 1.35; ≥ 0.8 needs ||Δ|| ≤ 0.51.
- That means a 27x (jar, node 1) to 110x (castle, node 2) reduction in ||Δ||, i.e. 750x to 12,000x in KL.
- In relative L2 of x0 (latent RMS ≈ 0.73, ||x0|| ≈ 390–400), Fast would have to match Base's RePaint x0 to within about:
  - 5% at node 0 (UNVERIFIED);
  - 1.7% at node 1 (now 39–47%);
  - 0.6% at node 2 (now 31–33%).
- The probability that an exact sampler can skip even one Base call at nodes 0–2 is at most about 1e-9 per transition, whatever the algorithm. This follows from the optimality of maximal coupling. K-candidate draft trees (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17691) only multiply it by K.

WHY SMALLER UNITS OR LOWER RESOLUTION DO NOT HELP
- Per latent frame ("frame-level"): ||Δ|| is divided by √3, giving 21–86. Still no lookahead.
- At the plan resolution (576x304, latent 38x72), d shrinks to 0.45x, so ||Δ|| shrinks only about 0.67x.
- Per position (16 dims): acceptance of 0.6–0.96, which is exact and useful, but it gives no lookahead. The next Base mean is a global function of the whole state, and "all 18,444 positions accepted" has probability Π(1−TV_p) ≈ 0.

STRUCTURAL CAUSE
- Fast is DMD-distilled; its x0 at high noise is a sample-like image. Base is undistilled; its x0 is E[x | z], a blurry posterior mean.
- So ||x0_F − x0_B||² is about tr Cov[x | z_k], which is large at high noise even if Fast's video marginal equalled Base's.
- The two path measures are therefore nearly singular. That makes kernel-level exactness the wrong granularity for a distilled/undistilled pair.
- The literature agrees:
  - exact coupling efficiency "degrades rapidly with dimension" (Bullo et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17691);
  - only 1.22x at K = 50 on a 4k-dim ImageNet LDM (Soen et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13426);
  - De Bortoli's Lemma 4.2, E[a] ≥ exp(−E||Δ||²/2), is vacuous at ||Δ||² ≈ 10³–10⁴.

THE ξ FLOOR (UNVERIFIED; measure it)
The target kernel is a mixture over the prefix noise ξ, which Fast never sees. The floor is ||Δ_ξ,k|| = (1−s')/s' · ||x0_B(z; ξ1) − x0_B(z; ξ2)||. It bounds acceptance for any ξ-blind draft, including Base itself run with an independent ξ. At node 2 (prefix SNR 0.2) it is plausibly above 1.35. Measuring it costs 2 Base calls per (chunk, node).

CONTEXT SPECULATION (CS-AR; UNVERIFIED)
To first order, ||Δ_ctx,k|| ≈ (1−s_{k+1})/s_{k+1} · ||J_k (1−s_k)(X_c − Xhat_c)||, where J_k is the Jacobian of Base's chunk x0 with respect to the prefix input.
- Node 0: 2e-4 × 0.067, i.e. about 0 (exactly 0 under T_H0).
- Node 1: 0.0627 × 0.2005, so ||Δ|| ≈ 0.0126 · g_1 · ||X_c − Xhat_c||. With ||X_c − Xhat_c|| ≈ 100–250, that is ||Δ|| ≈ 1.3–3.2 · g_1, where g_1 is Base's effective gain from prefix to chunk (unknown). Acceptance ≥ 0.5 needs g_1 ≲ 0.4–1.
- Node 2: 0.167 × 0.60, so ||Δ|| ≈ 0.1 · g_2 · ||X_c − Xhat_c||, which is probably ≫ 1.35. Node 2 is never speculated; in the lag-1 schedule it does not need to be.
- Irony: acceptance is high exactly because RePaint ignores the prefix at high noise, which is the same property that causes snap-back.

FREE BY-PRODUCTS
- The per-position TV maps (acc_pos, dnorm) are exact target-vs-draft disagreement measures at each node. They cost nothing and could serve as item-5's 'target-likelihood proxy'.
- The per-position reuse fraction (0.6–0.96) gives common random numbers with the Fast-only rollout, which makes paired spec-vs-Fast comparisons low-variance.
design.expected_speedup:
FORMULA
Adapted from De Bortoli et al. Prop. 4.1, counting one parallel verification round as one target call. That count is only valid with γ verifier GPUs, since the target is compute-bound and batched Base forwards fail in the camera path (NIGHT3:339).
- S = E[L̂] / (1 + γ·C_D/C_T)
- E[L̂] ≤ 1 + Σ_{j<γ} Π_{i≤j} a_i, with a_i ≤ 2Φ(−||Δ_i||/2) ≤ 1e-9.
- Cost ratio: C_D (Fast forward) ≈ 0.25–1.4 s. C_T (one Base CFG call) ≈ 3.4 s (chunk 1) to 35 s (chunk 12), mean ≈ 17.7 s. This fits t(n tokens) ≈ 0.164·n + 0.00215·n² s (n in thousands), from the measured 3.74 s at 18.4k tokens and 7.53 s at 32.3k.
- Result: S ≈ 0.93–0.99 for γ = 1, and lower for γ > 1 (wasted drafts plus rollback). Any exact scheme that uses Fast content drafts runs at 1x or slower than the target alone.

COST OF THE TARGET ITSELF
- One CFG-5 Base call per node, summed over chunks 1–12 = 2 × Σ_c τ_c ≈ 2 × 105 s ≈ 210 s per node. The logs give 213 s per node (spec_n12 denoise 426 s / 2 nodes; spec_n123 638 s / 3 nodes).

| Sampler (161 frames, 480p) | Exact w.r.t. | Base work on the critical path per chunk ↓ | Wall-clock (s) ↓ | GPUs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Base-70 whole clip (reference) | T* | – | 2834 (measured, jar s11) | 1 |
| T_H target-only, sequential | T_H | 3 CFG calls (6τ) | ≈735–750 (measured analogue: spec_n123 748–752) | 2 |
| SPEC-AR (specstep, per-position) | T_H | 6τ | ≈750–770 (est.; 0.95–1.0x) | 2 |
| PathSpec-AR, γ≥2, Fast drafts | T_H | ≈6τ (E[L̂] ≈ 1) | ≥ SPEC-AR | 2+γ |
| T_H0 exact parallel: CFG branches on 2 GPUs, node 0 precomputed on a third GPU, Fast on a fourth | T_H0 | 2τ | ≈260–300 (est., UNVERIFIED) | 4 (GPUs 4–7) |
| CS-AR (lag-1 diagonal) with CFG-parallel | T_H0 | τ·(2 − a_1) | <u>≈150–250</u> (est.; needs a_1 measured) | 8 |
| plan→render v2 (biased) | none | 0 | **114–206** (measured) | 1 |

HOW TO READ THE TABLE
- Versus the target process alone, speculation with Fast drafts gives 0.93–1.0x.
- The only exact speed-ups are:
  - about 2.5–2.9x from parallelising the target itself (no speculation);
  - with 8 GPUs and a node-1 context acceptance a_1 ≈ 1, a further ≤ 2x from CS-AR.
- With our 4 GPUs, CS-AR brings nothing beyond the CFG-parallel schedule. The diagonal needs 4 concurrent full CFG calls, which equals the 2τ per chunk of CFG-parallel.
- Versus Base-70: the exact T_H0 sampler would be about 10x cheaper (≈280 s vs 2834 s), but it samples T_H0, not T*.
- Versus plan→render: it is 1.3–2.6x slower, and probably worse visually, because of RePaint layout snap-back. That is UNVERIFIED until a specstep or target-only video exists.
- Block verification (Sun et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10444; Soen et al. 2026) cannot help. It optimises joint acceptance within a block, and the first transition is already capped at 1 − TV ≈ 0.

design.risks:
1. No speed-up exists with Fast as the draft. The professor may expect one from 'speculative sampling'.
   - Mitigation: present the bound, the logged numbers and the structural reason (distilled vs undistilled kernels), and show that the literature agrees: Bullo 2026 on dimension, Soen 2026 with 1.22x at K = 50.
2. Exactness to a bad target. T_H inherits chunk-wise RePaint layouts: prefix SNR 0.0002 / 0.067 / 0.20 leads to snap-back to frame 0 and an ignored camera action (NIGHT3:136, 148, 160). Fast's node 3 sees the clean prefix and may partly repair this (UNVERIFIED; no specstep video yet).
   - Exactness is only valuable if T_H0 scores near Base-70 in the item-4 batches.
3. Claim creep. 'Unbiased' must always name the target, e.g. 'exact w.r.t. T_H'.
   - Chunk 0 and node 3 are Fast.
   - It is NOT exact w.r.t. Base-70 or Base's conditionals.
   - Combining specstep with hints or a plan leaves the law equal to K_T's; it is not an exact plan→render.
   - The legacy --policy spec, and any τ ≠ 1, threshold or Base-regeneration path, is biased.
4. RNG. Unseeded global CUDA generators for ξ and u mean each run is marginally exact but the batches are not i.i.d. Whether the default CUDA seed is constant in this build is UNVERIFIED. Fix before the P5 batches.
5. Out-of-memory and co-tenancy. --resident with both experts predicts about 90 GB at the 39-latent last window. The 04:41 CDT crash came from a foreign 57 GB process on the same GPU. The Base-70 reference is 2834 s on one GPU, not the ~600 s quoted in the task.
6. Numerics. μT is computed in bf16 and is nondeterministic across runs, so exactness holds only w.r.t. the as-computed kernel.
   - Expect only bf16-level differences in the null test.
   - Residual checks can only detect errors larger than that noise.
7. KV rollback (lookahead variants). Fast's KV cache must be restored to exactly the committed prefix: sink/window eviction and cross-attention flags included. A silent mismatch breaks A5.
8. CS-AR is speculative in both senses.
   - The node-1 context acceptance is unknown and could be around 0 if Base's prefix gain g_1 ≳ 1.
   - It needs 8 GPUs to beat the simple CFG-parallel schedule.
   - Its high acceptance comes from the same prefix-blindness that makes the target poor.
9. Evaluation power. 8 seeds per arm cannot separate moderate drift-rate differences, and Base's own variance is large (DINO 0.29–0.75). Use ≥16 seeds and the per-run residual statistics for the exactness check.
10. Alternative 'exact' framings define the target through the verifier.
   - Example: a Base-score-tilted Fast process, sampled by redrawing from Fast on rejection; SDVG's regenerate-with-target law w·p_D + (1 − E w)·p_T is another.
   - These are cheap and exactly characterised but circular for item 4. If used, the drift judge must be held out from the acceptance score.

issues: Verdict: I could not refute the core claim. The in-order SPEC_AR loop with gamma=1 and per-position reflection coupling is exact with respect to the T_H path law, as coded in /home/hk28965/specwm/lingbot-world-v2/specwm/spec_v0.py lines 466-490 under --policy never --start 1 with defaults ctx=0, bguide=0, no hint/tex/kv-mem/fast-lora/polish/seam. What I checked line by line: (a) the Base mean is taken at the pre-transition state ZS[ci]['z'][-1] (L477), not at the proposed z. (b) Fast's mean is computed before eps, u or xi are drawn, so it cannot peek. (c) eps is recovered as (z-muD)/s, logr is summed over the 16 channels in fp32 (L481), there is one u per position (L482), and e is normalised per position; the reflection muT + s(eps - 2(e.eps)e) matches De Bortoli et al. Alg. 4 / Prop. 3.1 (https://arxiv.org/html/2501.05370v2). I also re-derived that p(Ry)=q(y). (d) Draws from the CPU stream g do not depend on accept/reject outcomes. (e) The expert boundary is 947 (/home/hk28965/specwm/lingbot-world/wan/configs/wan_i2v_A14B.py:36), so node 0 uses the high expert and nodes 1-2 the low expert, as stated. (f) CFG is 5 and camera_WM is empty for both test tasks. (g) A5 holds in order: in /home/hk28965/specwm/lingbot-world-v2/wan/modules/model_fast.py:133-170 eviction only fires when current_end > global_end_index, so it happens once per chunk whichever node calls first, and attention uses cache[_st:local_start] plus the fresh keys. The node-3 finish is therefore the same in the spec arm and the target-only arm. The problems below are in the auxiliary claims and the add-ons.

RNG claim is backwards (MEDIUM-1 misdiagnosed). No torch.manual_seed or torch.cuda.manual_seed exists in spec_v0, binding_v1/v2 or either wan tree. xi (torch.randn_like(pref) on dev1, L332) and u (torch.rand_like(logr) on dev0, L482) come from the default CUDA generators, which PyTorch seeds nondeterministically: getDefaultCUDAGenerator() calls .seed() -> getNonDeterministicRandom(true) (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytorch/pytorch/main/aten/src/ATen/cuda/CUDAGeneratorImpl.cpp; installed torch version not checked). So runs with different --seed are independent, not 'not i.i.d.'. The real defects are different: no run can be reproduced, a rerun after OOM gives a different video, and the spec arm and target-only arm cannot share xi, so paired common random numbers are impossible. The proposed G(seed,c,k,stream) fix is still right. Note that it also breaks CRN with existing Fast-only runs, which use one sequential g (chunk_noise followed by 3 eps draws per chunk).

The T_H0 argument that the change is 'below bf16 resolution' is false. base_flow casts the window to bf16 (L204). The prefix term (1-s0)X is about 1.5e-4 per entry. The bf16 ulp is <= 3e-4 whenever |s0*xi| < 2^-4, which covers about 5% of N(0,1) entries, so those entries carry the prefix at or above half an ulp. For all other entries, rounding a continuous random xi acts as dither: E[Q(s0*xi + delta) - Q(s0*xi)] is approximately delta. The patch embedding sums 64 entries per token, so the prefix signal reaches the network in expectation. T_H0 is therefore a genuinely different target. Exactness with respect to T_H0 is fine, but T_H0 ≈ T_H is UNVERIFIED. The item-6 speed-up 'node-0 calls off the critical path' is exact only for T_H0. That conflicts with the recommendation to report 'exact w.r.t. T_H'.

A5 is violated by the existing Fast KV code under the CS-AR and PathSpec-AR schedules. The claim that node-0-2 forwards 'leave no state behind' is literally false: the first call for a chunk rolls the cache destructively (clone-shift) and every call rewrites global_end_index and local_end_index. Concrete trace of CS-AR on the single cache in binding_v2 after the cache is full (c >= 5): (1) the speculative chunk c+1 forward (muD or node 2 at zs) rolls the cache, evicting the oldest 3 non-sink frames. (2) Chunk c's node-3 finish then takes the else-branch with local_start = S - 6f and attends over [0, S-6f). That is 6 sink frames plus only 6 past frames instead of 9. X_c is computed with one chunk of context missing, so the law of X_c differs from T_H: this is bias. The same holds for PathSpec-AR's 'optimistic Fast commit ... rollback Fast KV to exactly st.X'. The rollback needs a snapshot of the whole cache (about 21-23 GiB: 40 layers x 27,666 tokens x 5120 x K/V x bf16), which the design does not specify. The proposed A5 check (x0_F(z_3) with and without the preceding same-chunk forwards) cannot detect this cross-chunk failure.

The null test (C1) is wrong as specified. For one transition, n = 295,104 coordinates, so SE(mean) = 1/sqrt(n) = 0.0018 and SE(var) = sqrt(2/n) = 0.0026. The stated per-transition tolerances (0 ± 0.0003, 1 ± 0.0005) are the pooled tolerances over all 36 transitions. A correct implementation would fail the per-transition mean test about 87% of the time. More importantly, r = (z' - muT)/s' is measured against whichever muT was actually used. It therefore only checks the coupling algebra and is blind to exactly the failures that matter: a muT evaluated at a stale state or context (A4), a corrupted Fast KV (A5), or cond_cache reuse. The null must either recompute muT independently at the realised state and context with the same xi, or compare the spec batch with the target-only batch.

The CS-AR schedule is internally inconsistent. At tick τ it runs 'node 2 of chunk c' and 'verify node 1 of chunk c+1' together. The verification needs X_c = FastX0(z_3^c), which exists only after node 2 of chunk c plus the node-3 finish and the commit (about 2 extra Fast forwards). The verification belongs to tick τ+1, and base_mean for node 2 of chunk c+1 also has to wait for X_c, so the claimed overlap is smaller than drawn. A separate problem is that chunk c's finish and chunk c+1's speculative Fast forwards need two different KV states at the same time, i.e. two cache copies or two Fast replicas; the GPU budget does not include these. Lemma 3 itself is fine: Z' comes from fresh (eps1, u1a), and the stale mean muS may depend on discarded zs, as A2 allows.

Target description errors. (1) The Fast KV is 18 latent frames in total (kv_size = frame_seqlen * local_attn_size with fast_win=18, sink=6; image2video.py:369 and model_fast.py:122,138), not '6 sink + 18 window'. Once full, a chunk's finish sees 6 sink frames, 9 recent frames and its own 3. (2) 'Fast receives integer timesteps 999/937/833/625': target_flow passes sch.timesteps[argmin|sigma - s|] from binding_v2, which is harmless but not verified to be integers. (3) Latent hazard: base_cond caches by (F, j, area), not by prefix content (L194-201). With --ctx > 0, a lookahead or stale-context call would cache the decoded stale frame, and the true-context verification would reuse it, which violates A4. The default ctx=0 is safe; this must be asserted if lookahead is ever used with ctx.

Overclaims in the 'hard limit' and in item 5. The acceptance bound 2Φ(-||Δ||/2) is for coupling Fast's mean against a single xi-conditioned Gaussian component. The actual target kernel is the xi-mixture, and TV(draft, mixture) <= E_xi TV(draft, component_xi). 'Any exact scheme ... gains essentially no lookahead' is therefore not proven: other drafts, or coupling on (xi, z') jointly, are not excluded. The conclusion is probably still right given ||Δ|| >= 37, but it is not a theorem. Likewise, the 'free exact per-position TV map' is the TV to one xi-component. It is not the TV to the target kernel and not a likelihood, so as an item-5 target-likelihood proxy it is confounded by xi noise. The ||Δ|| figures come from states of the legacy biased chain, not from T_H states.

The guarantee is valid but says little about quality. T_H has never been run: Base CFG-5 x0-renoise on Fast's 4-node sigma grid, with RePaint prefix conditioning at prefix SNR 0.0002/0.067/0.20, and a Fast finish. It belongs to the chunk-wise RePaint family that NIGHT3_NOTES.md:136,148,160 documents with snap-back, seams and ignored camera. 'Unbiased' only guarantees equality in law with this unmeasured sampler, not with Base-70. Item 3 needs a target-only T_H batch (--specstep 2) evaluated with the item-4 protocol before 'exact' carries any meaning. Separately, /home/hk28965/specwm/paper/action_items_status.md:9 still describes the superseded biased rejection loop with at most 4 tries. It must be updated before any exactness claim; --spec-tries is now dead code.

Nothing else biases the output. I found no data-dependent stopping, retries, truncation or fallback in the --specstep path under --policy never. The legacy rejection loop with at most 4 tries and a fallback, and the --policy spec tau threshold (L544-566), would bias the output but are not reached. The same goes for --policy every/verify/always, which replace x0 with base_repaint_chunk. The code must therefore assert --policy never whenever specstep is on. Dropping crashed runs from a batch is harmless only if the crash does not depend on the content (true for OOM caused by other processes; any NaN or quality filter would add selection bias).

At the sigma 0.937 state it is 19-84, and at the sigma 0.833 state it is 47-203 (castle is the high end); the design gives 37-148. In the best observed chunk (||Delta|| = 19.4), P(accept whole state) = 2*Phi(-9.7), about 3e-22. The correct statement is "at most about 1e-21". It is still effectively zero, so the conclusion stands.

The relative-L2 figures are shifted by one node. The design quotes 39-47% at node 1 and 31-33% at node 2, but those are the legacy values at the sigma 0.833 and sigma 0.625 states. At T_H's node-1 state (sigma 0.937) the measured rel is 0.17-0.78; at the node-2 state (sigma 0.833) it is 0.14-0.47. The required thresholds are right: with ||x0|| about 390, 1.35/(0.2 x 390) = 1.7% and 1.35/(0.6 x 390) = 0.58%. The measured values are still 10-40x too large.

The 59-96% per-position reuse range is off. Measured on jar: 58-91%, never 96%. On castle, the legacy 64-dim per-token acceptance at sigma 0.833 was 0.21-0.42 (||Delta|| 113-203). That predicts a per-position RMS |Delta_p| of 0.83-1.49 and acceptance of about 0.45-0.68 (UNVERIFIED prediction). A realistic range is about 45-91%.

Arithmetic for the full-prefix parallel target (T_H0, GPUs 4-7). I fitted Base cost per forward as cost(n) = 0.243n + 0.00542n^2 s for an n-latent window. It matches 3.74 s at n=12, 7.53 s at n=21, and the legacy total t_denoise of 638 s for 36 CFG calls. Target alone: 638 + 24 swaps x 0.65 s + cond 48 + Fast about 25 + VAE = about 740 s (the design's figure is fine). Critical path when each CFG pair is split across 2 GPUs: 2 x sum_c cost(3c+3) = 211 s, plus Fast about 25, plus VAE about 10, gives about 250 s. The node-0 GPU must do 2cost(n) per chunk, while the main path takes 2cost(n) + 1.8 s per chunk. So node 0 runs at the same throughput as the main path and falls behind from about chunk 6; it keeps up only thanks to the head start from chunk 0. If the conditioning prepare (48 s: T5 on CPU plus VAE encode per new F) runs on that GPU, it gates the path and the total is about 300-310 s (2.4x). So 2.5-2.9x holds only if conditioning is precomputed on the Fast GPU or the CPU.

For the config actually queued (c9), the same parallel layout gives: per chunk, 2 x 3.74 + 1.8 + about 0.3 = about 9.6 s; 12 chunks plus chunk 0 plus VAE = about 130 s, vs about 317 s target-only, so about 2.4x (UNVERIFIED). This is in the same range as plan->render (114-206 s), but plan->render uses 1-2 GPUs, not 4.

The parallel speed-up does not come from speculative sampling. The same CFG split and pipelining applies to the target-only arm and to Base-70 (the CFG split alone roughly halves Base-70's measured 2829-3111 s on one GPU; UNVERIFIED). In GPU-seconds it is worse: about 4 x 260 = 1040 vs about 740 for target-only. It must be reported as systems parallelism, not as an item-3 speed-up.

Feasibility and effort of the parallel target. spec_v0 has a single global live model and expert(), plus cur_expert, W, DLOCK and b1 conditioning, all on dev1 (spec_v0.py:141-209). The split needs 3 Base replicas: 2 low-expert (nodes 1,2) and 1 high-expert (node 0), so no swaps. Each also needs its own copies of the y and camera dit_cond tensors, and the forwards must be launched concurrently. Batching cond and uncond in one call is not an option, since batched forwards fail in the Plucker/camera path. There is a precedent for cross-device races: kv4 hit illegal memory accesses until synchronize() calls were added (NIGHT3, 9/27 22:30). Estimate: 1-2 days plus validation (UNVERIFIED). It needs all of GPUs 4-7, which the overnight kv4 and evaluation jobs currently hold. Host RAM (792 GB total, 502 GB free now) is fine only with a single process and no pinned weight copies; six pinned Base processes previously OOMed the host at 774 GB.

CS-AR cannot pay off on our 4 GPUs. With 3 Base GPUs and no CFG split, each call takes 2cost(n), which is the same per-chunk throughput as the non-speculative CFG-split path, so the gain is 0. On 8 GPUs the per-chunk path is cost + about 2.7 + (1-alpha) x cost, vs 2cost + 1.8. At chunk 12 (cost 17.7 s) that is 1.8x at alpha = 1, 1.27x at alpha = 0.5, and below 1x at alpha = 0. Those 8 GPUs would include 0-3, which are not ours by default. Acceptance also needs Base's node-1 x0 to change by less than 1.7% relative L2 (||delta x0|| <= 6.7) when the last prefix chunk goes from x0_F(z_2) to x0_F(z_3). Acceptance is high only where Base ignores the prefix, which is exactly where T_H shows the snap-back failure. Nobody has measured this (UNVERIFIED).

The design does not consider the frozen-target draft, which is De Bortoli et al.'s main draft (Alg. 3 with the frozen target; https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.05370, verified via the v2 HTML: Alg. 4 is the reflection coupling, Prop. 3.1 gives TV = 2Phi(||Delta||/(2 sigma)) - 1, and the paper says it is "not directly applicable to deterministic samplers"). It also fails here. Whole-state acceptance would need Base's x0 to move less than 1.7% between sigma 0.94 and 0.83. NIGHT3 probe B shows Base's x0 is still far from final after the high-noise steps (DINO 0.27-0.83). Their reported NFE savings come from 35-100 fine steps, not a 4-node schedule.

The "free per-position TV map as a target-likelihood proxy" (item 5) is not free. It needs 3 Base CFG calls per chunk over the full window: about 24 s per chunk for c9, and about 53 s per chunk at chunk 12 with the full prefix. As a verifier signal it costs more than a whole plan->render run.

The residual-test tolerances in C1 are wrong per transition. Over 295,104 coordinates, the standard error of the mean is 0.0018 and of the variance is 0.0026. The quoted +/-0.0003 and +/-0.0005 are the values pooled over all 36 transitions (10.6M coordinates). Applied per transition, they would flag correct runs as biased (about 6-sigma false alarms).

T_H0's "below bf16 resolution" claim needs a caveat. The prefix term is about 1.5e-4, against a half-ulp of about 2e-3 for |xi| in [0.5, 1). That still changes the bf16 rounding of about 4% of entries, and it is fully resolved for |xi| below about 0.04 (about 3% of entries). So node 0 is not bitwise independent of the prefix. That is acceptable because T_H0 is declared as a change of target, but it must not be described as identical to T_H.

Verified facts: Base-70 on one GPU takes 2829-3111 s (jar s11 2833.7 s, s1234 2829.1 s, s22 3110.5 s), so the task text's ~600 s is wrong for one GPU. The Base boundary is 0.947 (wan_i2v_A14B.py:36), so node 0 uses the high expert and nodes 1-2 the low expert, as the design says. An expert swap costs about 0.65 s (23 swaps = about 15 s), not 2-3 s. The legacy n123 policy-spec run took about 750 s (749.6 s for jar s1234).

design.name: LSAR: Lookahead Speculative AR sampling with whole-state reflection coupling (exact with respect to an explicit hybrid chunk-AR Base target), plus a no-go analysis for speed at chunk dimensionality
design.summary:
WHAT IT IS. An exact speculative sampler that runs over the global order of stochastic transitions (chunk c, node k). Each round has four steps:
1. Fast drafts L transitions ahead from the true state.
2. Base computes the kernel means for every drafted Base-owned transition. These run concurrently, up to W at once, on GPUs 4-7.
3. A whole-state reflection maximal coupling (De Bortoli et al., Alg. 4, https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.05370) keeps the longest prefix of drafted transitions that it accepts.
4. The first rejected transition is replaced by its reflection, and the next round starts from there.
With L=0 the algorithm reduces to the current per-latent-position specstep (spec_v0.py:473-486), which is exact per transition. The output law equals an explicitly defined hybrid chunk-AR target T_V (Base-RePaint CFG-5 kernels at nodes 0-2 of chunks 1-12; Fast at node 3 and for chunk 0). It is NOT Base-70.

SPEED VERDICT (from our own logs, no new GPU runs). The source is the 5 probe runs in /home/hk28965/specwm/lingbot-world-v2/specwm_out/spec_v0/{sand_filling_up_jar,sandcastle_wave_impact}/probe_s*/spec_v0.json (60 chunks). Their logged per-token log-ratio gives KL(draft kernel || Base kernel) of 0.27-4.1 nats per 64-dim token. Summed over the 4,611 tokens of a chunk this is 1,259-19,085 nats per chunk transition, so whole-chunk acceptance is at most 10^-138. The measured per-token acceptance (0.20-0.74) matches the Gaussian theory to within 0.02-0.05, which validates the arithmetic.
- The expected extra accepted lookahead is therefore 0 for any L.
- The best achievable wall-clock is 1.00x against the target alone, with draft and target running concurrently.
- As currently coded (sequential) it is about 0.94x.
Two further arguments point the same way:
- Coupling inequality: any exact scheme accepts a Fast chunk with probability at most 1-TV. Fast-only and Base-70 clip flicker do not overlap at all (jar 47.9-54.5 vs 4.3-13.9; castle 28.5-32.4 vs 15.1-25.1), so TV is close to 1 (small sample).
- Self-drafting on Base (the literal De Bortoli / Soen mechanism) scales as K proportional to sqrt(d). Calibrated on Soen et al.'s ImageNet-LDM point (12,288 dims: 1.22x at K=50, 2.25x at K=250; https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13426), our 295k-dim chunk would need about 245 steps for 1.22x and about 1,225 for 2.25x. Both are a net loss against a 16- or 70-step target.
- The only exact regime with more than 1.5x is a target in which Base owns 200 or fewer numbers per chunk transition (for example per-frame channel means). At that point it is barely a Base target.

TARGET QUALITY WARNING (new finding from the logs). Run bg1_n01 (--bguide 1 --bguide-nodes 0,1, policy never, CFG 5, full prefix; spec_v0.py:466-472) is, line by line, a target-only sample of T_{V={0,1}}. It froze: motion about 2 vs Base 16, stutter, 552 s (NIGHT3_NOTES.md, Sep 25 12:05 AM). T_{0,1,2} is expected to be at least as mean-seeking, so an 'unbiased' specstep will most likely reproduce this freeze.

RECOMMENDATION.
- Report item 3 as: exact algorithm + proof + no-go numbers.
- Run L=0 concurrently, together with a target-only null batch (implementation check for item 4).
- Get speed only from the target definition: node-0 prefix-free precompute and block-causal Base-KV at nodes 1-2, estimated about 210-570 s but quality UNVERIFIED. The alternative is controlled bias (item 5), with plan->render (114-206 s) as the practical line.
design.target_definition:
NOTATION
- s = (s0, s1, s2, s3) = (0.99980, 0.93727, 0.83306, 0.62469). These are the binding's shift-5 1000-step grid at indices 0/250/500/750. This is also exactly the lightx2v/Self-Forcing 4-step grid.
- Chunk c = 0..12 (N=13, 153 frames); chunk latent z in R^{16x3x58x106} (d = 295,104).
- X_<c = committed prefix.
- x0F(z,k | X_<c) = Fast's node-k x0, using its KV cache (sink 6 + window 18).
- x0B(z,k | X_<c, zeta) = base_x0_at (spec_v0.py:329-333): one Base-A14B forward at CFG 5 over the window [prefix re-noised as (1-s_k)X_<c + s_k*zeta, z], at t = 1000*s_k. The expert is high if t >= 947 (node 0) and low otherwise. Conditioning: start image + poses of frames 0..F-1, empty prompt, Wan default negative prompt.

DEFAULT TARGET T_H = T_{V,kappa,g} (the law the current code samples, per the audit):
- V = {(c,k): c=1..12, k in {0,1,2}}.
- kappa = RePaint window with the full prefix (ctx 0).
- g = Fast final map.
Generative definition:
- Chunk 0: X_0 = Fast 4-node sampler (x0-renoise), seeded CPU generator.
- For c = 1..12:
  - z_{c,0} = eps_{c,0} ~ N(0,I) (same keyed draw as Fast-only).
  - For k = 0,1,2: draw zeta_{c,k} ~ N(0,I) (independent, keyed). Then z_{c,k+1} ~ N(m_{c,k}, s_{k+1}^2 I) with:
    - m_{c,k} = (1-s_{k+1}) * x0B(z_{c,k},k | X_<c, zeta_{c,k}) if (c,k) in V;
    - m_{c,k} = (1-s_{k+1}) * x0F(z_{c,k},k | X_<c) if (c,k) is not in V.
  - X_c = g(z_{c,3}) := x0F(z_{c,3},3 | X_<c), with y restored to the plain y. X_c is committed to Fast's KV cache and to the Base prefix list.
- Law: P_T(X) = P_F(X_0) * prod_{c>=1} ∫ N(z0;0,I) * prod_{k=0..2} E_zeta[N(z_{k+1}; m_{c,k}, s_{k+1}^2 I)] * delta(X_c - g(z3)) dz.
Properties:
- The Fast draft at nodes 0-2 has zero influence on this law.
- T_H is neither Base-70 nor Base's true conditional p_B(X_c | X_<c).
- Prefix weight 1-s_k is 2.0e-4, 0.063 and 0.167 at nodes 0, 1 and 2. At node 0 this is at the level of one bf16 rounding step on a small fraction of entries (Base casts its input to bf16 in base_flow), so Base effectively re-draws the layout from the image and poses. This is the snap-back mechanism, NIGHT3_NOTES.md:136.
- Evidence on quality: bg1_n01 (spec_v0.py:466-472 with bguide=1, CFG 5, ctx 0) is a target-only sample of T_{V={0,1}}. It froze and stuttered on castle 4321 and jar 9999.

VARIANTS (same algorithm and proof; only the target changes):
1. T_B, Fast-free. Add chunk 0 to V (needs an L=0 branch in base_x0_at). Add a Base-owned final transition z_{c,3} -> N((1-s_min)*x0B, s_min^2 I) and set g = identity. Fast then has no influence on the output law, and the cost is at least that of the target alone.
2. T_H', node-0 prefix-free. The node-0 Base window uses pure noise zeta in place of (1-s0)X_<c + s0*zeta (a difference of 2e-4*X). Node-0 means then depend only on keyed eps_{c,0}, zeta, image and poses, so all 12 of them can be precomputed in parallel on spare GPUs. This is a target change that is practically invisible and it shortens the critical path by about 1/3.
3. T_H-KV. Nodes 1-2 use kv_x0 (block-causal Base low expert, clean-prefix KV cache, spec_v0.py:352-358) at 3.5-3.9 s per CFG call instead of about 17-18 s for RePaint. The high expert cannot use a clean prefix (NIGHT3:5), so node 0 stays RePaint. Quality UNVERIFIED.
4. T_K. A chunk-conditional Base chain with K >= 16 noise-retaining steps: z' ~ N(a_k z + b_k x0B, c_k^2 I), DDPM/eta-type. This is the only per-chunk kernel that is Base-faithful (16-step RePaint corrections were stable). It still ignores the camera and snaps back (always16, NIGHT3 10:40 PM). Cost is about 2,200-3,500 s. A Fast draft needs the same kernel form, with Fast evaluated off its 4 nodes (OOD).
5. T_u. Split z = (u,v) with an orthonormal transform (Haar low-pass u, detail v). Base owns the u-kernel N((1-s')P_u x0B, s'^2 I_u). Fast owns v given the state. Only u is verified.

Exactness is always stated as 'with respect to T_{V,kappa,g}'. Never claim 'unbiased with respect to Base'.
design.algorithm_pseudocode:
```
# Keyed randomness (fixes audit bug: no global CUDA RNG). One torch.Generator per purpose,
# seeded from hash(seed, c, k, purpose), purpose in {epsD, zeta, U, eps0}.
# Transitions in global order tau = (c,k); Base-owned iff tau in V.

def draft_mean(y, pref, tau):   return (1 - s[k+1]) * x0F(y, k | pref)            # Fast, same code as the draft rollout
def target_mean(y, pref, tau):  return draft_mean(y, pref, tau) if tau not in V \
                                   else (1 - s[k+1]) * x0B(y, k | pref, zeta[tau])  # RePaint or KV, CFG = --spec-cfg

def couple_whole(yD, mD, mT, sp, U):            # Alg.4 (De Bortoli 2025), whole state, fp64 reductions
    xi = (yD - mD) / sp;  D = (mD - mT) / sp;  nD = ||D||
    logr = -(2 * <xi, D> + nD**2) / 2           # log N(yD; mT) / N(yD; mD)
    if log(U) <= min(0, logr): return yD, True
    e = D / nD;  return mT + sp * (xi - 2 * <e, xi> * e), False      # = yD - sp*(nD + 2<e,xi>) e

def couple_perpos(yD, mD, mT, sp, Upos):        # spec_v0.py:477-486; kernels factorise over the 18,444 positions
    xi = (yD - mD) / sp;  D = (mD - mT) / sp                          # [16,3,58,106]
    logr = -(2 * (xi*D).sum(0) + (D*D).sum(0)) / 2                   # per position
    acc = log(Upos) <= logr.clamp(max=0)
    e = D / ||D||_pos;  refl = mT + sp * (xi - 2 * (e*xi).sum(0) * e)
    return where(acc, yD, refl), bool(acc.all())

def LSAR(seed, L, W, mode):     # mode: 'perpos' (only when L == 0) or 'whole'
    X0 = chunk0_by_target();  commit(X0)       # Fast (T_H) or Base (T_B)
    tau = (1, 0);  z = eps0[1];  pref = [X0]
    while tau != END:
        # 1) DRAFT from the true state: frontier + L speculative transitions (Fast, sequential, GPU A)
        traj = [];  y, t, p = z, tau, pref;  snapKV = snapshot_fastKV() if crosses_chunk(tau, L) else None
        for j in range(L + 1):
            mD = draft_mean(y, p, t);  yD = mD + s[t.k+1] * epsD[t]
            traj.append((t, y, p, mD, yD));  y, t, p = advance(yD, t, p)   # node 3: X = g(y), speculative KV commit, next z = eps0[c+1]
        # 2) VERIFY concurrently (<= W Base forwards on GPUs B..; one process per GPU because batched camera path fails).
        #    The frontier target forward starts at the same time as the frontier draft forward (both need only z, pref).
        mT = parallel([target_mean(y, p, t) for (t, y, p, _, _) in traj if t in V])
        # 3) COUPLE in order and stop at the first transition whose output != draft
        for j, (t, y, p, mD, yD) in enumerate(traj):
            if t not in V:  out, ok = yD, True                               # identical kernels, Delta = 0
            elif mode == 'perpos' and L == 0:  out, ok = couple_perpos(yD, mD, mT[t], s[t.k+1], Upos[t])
            else:  out, ok = couple_whole(yD, mD, mT[t], s[t.k+1], U[t])
            z, tau, pref = advance_commit(out, t, pref)                    # real commit; X_c = g(z_{c,3})
            log(t, ||D||, logr, frac_pos_acc, ok)                          # free diagnostics (item 5/6)
            if not ok:  break                                              # discard traj[j+1:], their mT
        if snapKV:  restore_fastKV_to(pref)                                # undo speculative chunk commits
    return concat(pref)

# Modes: L=0 & 'perpos' = current specstep (+ concurrency). --spec-null: out = mT + s*epsD[t] (target-only arm, same keys).
# Self-drafting (item-2 baseline on T_K): draft_mean = a_k y + b_k x0B(z_n) from the last verified state (free drafter);
#   the first transition of each round then has Delta = 0 exactly.
```
design.unbiasedness_proof:
CLAIM. For any L >= 0, W >= 1 and mode, LSAR outputs X ~ P_T, where T = T_{V,kappa,g} is defined in target_definition.

ASSUMPTIONS (each one is necessary; breaking any one makes the result biased):
- A1, equal isotropic covariance. The draft and target kernels at every tau are N(., s_{k+1}^2 I) with the same s. This holds for x0-renoise on both sides. For noise-retaining target kernels the draft must be rewritten in the same (a z + b x0 + c xi) form.
- A2, exact target mean at the true state. m^T used in a coupling is computed at the state that actually holds after all earlier outputs. This holds for accepted speculative states because they equal the output bit for bit. The same tensor must be used in the test and in the reflection, and it must come from the same code path and precision as the target definition. Non-deterministic bf16 kernels are fine: the realised evaluation is the kernel draw.
- A3, keyed independent randomness. epsD[tau], U[tau], Upos[tau], zeta[tau] and eps0[c] are mutually independent N(0,I) or U[0,1] draws, each keyed only by (seed, tau, purpose), independent of every state. This requires dedicated generators; the current global CUDA RNG is unseeded (audit).
- A4, shared deterministic maps. The chunk output map g (Fast node-3 x0 with the plain y), KV commits and conditioning are identical functions of the state in the draft and target paths.
- A5, no hidden fallbacks. There are no try limits, tau thresholds, Base replacement policies or blends. Assert policy == never; the --bguide, --hint-lora and --plan-video paths must not change the target silently.
- A6. Given zeta, the target kernel is exactly Gaussian. The zeta-mixture is realised by drawing zeta first.

LEMMA 1 (single transition; Bou-Rabee et al. 2020; De Bortoli et al. 2025 Prop. 3.1, https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.05370). Let yD = mD + s*xi with xi ~ N(0,I) and U ~ U[0,1] independent. Output yD if U <= min(1, N(yD; mT, s^2)/N(yD; mD, s^2)); otherwise output mT + s(I - 2ee^T)xi with e = (mD - mT)/||mD - mT||. Then the output is distributed as N(mT, s^2 I), and P(output = yD) = 1 - TV = 2*Phi(-||mD - mT||/(2s)), which is the maximum possible.
Proof sketch. The accepted part has density min(p, q). The reflection is an isometry that swaps N(mD, s^2) and N(mT, s^2) on the two half-spaces separated by the bisecting hyperplane, so it maps the rejected part (p - q)_+ onto (q - p)_+. The two parts sum to q.

LEMMA 1' (per position). Given the state S_tau, both means are functions of S_tau only and both covariances are diagonal, so p(.|S) = prod_pos p_pos and q(.|S) = prod_pos q_pos. Apply Lemma 1 independently per position, with independent U_pos. The product of the outputs has the law prod_pos q_pos = q(.|S).

LEMMA 2 (identical kernels). If tau is not in V, or tau is a chunk-initial noise draw, or the step is the map g, then the draft and the target coincide, so outputting the draft is exact.

LEMMA 3 (lookahead / optional stopping). Fix a round that starts at tau0 with S_{tau0} ~ the target marginal. Let F_j be the sigma-field of all keyed randomness with keys <= tau0+j. Let J be the first j at which the coupling output differs from the draft.
Induction on j: suppose the outputs at tau0+1..tau0+j-1 all equal the draft. Then the drafted state at tau0+j-1 is the true state, so by A2 the Base mean computed on it is the target mean at the true state. By Lemma 1, 1' or 2, S_{tau0+j} ~ Q_{tau0+j}(. | S_{tau0+j-1}), whether or not the draft is accepted.
The event {J = j} is F_j-measurable, so J is a stopping time. The randomness keyed beyond tau0+J is independent of F_J (A3). Its earlier use to build discarded speculative states and Base evaluations never entered any decision that is measurable with respect to F_J, so reusing it in the next round is legitimate (A3).
By the strong Markov property of the target chain, the concatenated output path has the law of the target Markov chain.

TERMINATION. Every round advances by at least one transition, because the rejected transition's output is itself a valid target draw.

THEOREM. By induction over rounds, the full path (z_{c,k})_{c,k} has the law of the T-chain, so X = (X_0, g(z_{c,3})) ~ P_T.

COROLLARIES.
- (i) Because of Lemma 3, the Fast draft never affects the law; it affects only the path, through common random numbers. So the target-only rollout (--spec-null: z' = mT + s*epsD, same keys) is equal in law, and is the correct null batch for testing the implementation.
- (ii) Exactness holds only with respect to T. With T_H, node 3 and chunk 0 are Fast. With T_B, Fast has no influence on the output law.
- (iii) Mixing the two modes is NOT exact: using the whole-state test to decide continuation and then per-position outputs in the reject branch does not produce the residual law. The reject branch must be the whole-state reflection, or per-position must be used for both the decision and the output (continue iff every position is accepted).
- (iv) The whole-state reflection output differs from the draft only along e: y' = yD - s(||Delta|| + 2<e,xi>)e. In other words it keeps Fast's noise, not Fast's content.

- Lookahead needs the whole next state to be unchanged. Base is bidirectional over the window and Fast attends across the whole chunk, so a single rejected position changes every later mean. Per-position acceptance therefore gives no lookahead:

PRECISION A DRAFTER WOULD NEED for whole-chunk acceptance 0.5 (||Delta|| <= 1.35, KL <= 0.91 nat):
- The relative x0 error must be at most 4.3% / 1.43% / 0.48% at nodes 0 / 1 / 2.

- Break-even for lookahead L=1: a >= t_F/t_B, i.e. a >= 0.077 (RePaint, 18 s) or a >= 0.38 (KV, 3.7 s). That corresponds to ||Delta|| <= 3.5 or 1.8 (KL <= 6.2 or 1.6 nats per chunk transition).

MODEL-FREE BOUND (coupling inequality). Any exact scheme that keeps a whole Fast chunk has P <= 1 - TV(P_F(X_c|.), P_T(X_c|.)). A single statistic already separates Fast-only from Base-70 (clip flicker, lower is Base-like, from temporal_eval*.json):
- jar: 47.9-54.5 vs 4.3-13.9;
- castle: 28.5-32.4 vs 15.1-25.1.
The ranges are disjoint, which suggests TV close to 1. With 2-3 samples per arm this is evidence, not proof. Plan->render overlaps Base on flicker (jar 13.2-20.6, castle 10.5-18.4), so this bound does not rule it out.

SELF-DRAFTING (the literal item-2 baseline on a K-step Base chunk chain). Heuristic scaling:
- Frozen or free drift gives Delta about h * grad(b) * xi, so KL_step is proportional to d/K^2, and equal efficiency needs K proportional to sqrt(d). This is consistent with Lemma 4.2 and with the martingale identity E||x0hat_{t'} - x0hat_t||^2 = mmse(t) - mmse(t').
- Anchor: Soen et al. ImageNet-LDM (latent 64x64x3 = 12,288 dims; eps 0.5, gamma 7, block verification): 1.22x at K=50, 1.57x at 100, 2.25x at 250, 3.01x at 500, 3.91x at 1000 (verified in the arXiv HTML, https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13426).
- Our chunk is 4.9x their dimension scale: K=70 corresponds to 14 on their scale, and K=16 to 3.3. We would need K of about 245 for 1.22x and about 1,225 for 2.25x.
- Whole clip (4.03M dims, 18x): K=70 corresponds to 3.9.
- Expect E[L^] of about 1.0-1.1 at K = 16-70 (UNVERIFIED; exponent heuristic). Bullo et al. also report that exact coupling efficiency degrades quickly with dimension (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17691).

FORMULA. Per round, S = E[progress] * (t_B + t_own) / (t_B + L*t_F + t_own), where E[progress] = sum_{j=0..L} prod_{i<=j} a_i. With the measured whole-chunk a < 1e-138 this gives E[progress] = 1, so S = t_B / (t_B + L*t_F) <= 1. The optimum is L* = 0, with draft and target running concurrently.

R1 (highest). The target, not the algorithm, determines quality. T_{0,1}'s target-only sample (bg1_n01) froze. Mechanism: posterior-mean x0 at sigma >= 0.83, re-noised with fresh noise, with the prefix nearly invisible to Base (prefix weight 2e-4 / 0.063 / 0.167 at nodes 0 / 1 / 2). An 'unbiased' specstep will therefore probably look worse than plan->render. Chunk-wise Base ignores the camera under every conditioning tried (NIGHT3 Sep 25 1:00 AM), so no AR target built from chunk-wise Base is known to be Base-like. Mitigation: always state 'exact with respect to T', and pick the target with the item-4 protocol.

R2. Expectation mismatch: item 3 gives no speed-up (at best 1.00x). Present the coupling inequality, the measured KL (1,259-19,085 nats per chunk transition) and the d_u trade-off as the result, not as a failure.

R3. The probe KL was measured on Fast-only states, not on states reached under the target. Values on target states may differ (UNVERIFIED), but the margin is more than 100 orders of magnitude. P1 logs the true values at no extra cost.

R4. Unseeded global CUDA RNG (zeta, U) leaves the seeds non-i.i.d. and breaks the item-4 comparison. Fix before any batch run (P1a).

R5. Memory and ops:
- --resident gives about 90 GB at late windows (OOM).
- Host RAM: at most 3 Base processes pinning experts.
- Batched Base forwards fail in the camera (plucker) path, so W > 1 needs one process per GPU, each holding the Base weights.
- Only GPUs 4-7 are ours; the GPUs are shared and co-tenant OOMs have occurred.

R6. Silent bias from implementation shortcuts: the node-3 or chunk-0 claim, the legacy --policy spec (biased residual), bguide or hint paths altering the kernel, whole-state decision combined with per-position output (not exact, Corollary iii), speculative KV writes not rolled back, and reuse of a Base evaluation computed on a state that is not bit-identical. Mitigations: assertions, the Fast-as-target identity test, the null arm, and the residual z-score check.

R7. Numerics. The whole-state log r sums over 295k dims, so compute it in fp64. Base runs in bf16 and may be non-deterministic; the realised evaluation is the kernel draw, so the same tensor must be used for the test and for the reflection.

R8. The self-drafting scaling (K proportional to sqrt(d)) is a heuristic calibrated on one external data point (Soen et al., ImageNet-LDM 12,288 dims). The true exponent for our model is UNVERIFIED; P6c measures it.

R9. T_u assumes a white mismatch, which is optimistic. If the Fast-vs-Base difference is concentrated in low frequencies (layout), KL_u is larger and the speed-up disappears.

R10. Literature. Soen et al. 2606.13426 and Bullo et al. 2609.17691 are recent preprints. Soen's LDM numbers and Prop. 3.2 were checked in the arXiv HTML. The window L for De Bortoli's Table 1 and any official code are UNVERIFIED or absent. The ~600 s Base-70 figure in the task conflicts with the 2,829 s single-GPU measurement.

verdicts.severity: medium: the core math is sound and every gap can be fixed, but the claim "for any L, this pseudocode" is false as written for L >= 1. The recommended L=0 per-position run is exact w.r.t. T_H once flags are pinned.
issues: WHAT SURVIVES (checked, not refuted). (a) Lemma 1: the map x -> mT + R(x - mD) with R = I - 2ee^T gives ||y-mT|| = ||x-mD|| and ||y-mD|| = ||x-mT||, so q(y) = p(x). It therefore pushes (p-q)_+ onto (q-p)_+, and adding min(p,q) gives q. Acceptance 1-TV = 2*Phi(-||D||/(2s)) is correct. Corollary (iv) algebra is correct. (b) The current specstep at spec_v0.py:473-486 implements exactly this: yD = (1-s)x0 + s*eps uses the same x0 tensor as muD; logr and clamp are correct; the reflection is correct; clamp_min(1e-12) guards D = 0. SPEC_NODES {0,1,2} indexes NODES [0,1,2,3] correctly. --spec-tries is parsed but never used, so there is no retry loop. (c) The per-position factorisation holds given (S, zeta) (A6). (d) The lookahead is exact in principle, and a simpler proof exists than Lemma 3's optional-stopping argument. Every committed transition t is produced by the same function Phi_t(true S_{t-1}, epsD[t], U[t], zeta[t]), whatever L is and whichever round commits it. So LSAR(L) is pathwise identical to LSAR(0) under the same keys, and no strong Markov argument is needed. (e) Probe numbers reproduce from the probe spec_v0.json files. Per-token KL: jar 0.92-0.93 / 0.25-0.30 / 1.06-1.19; castle 0.96-0.99 / 0.86-0.95 / 3.69-4.59. The run with bguide=1, bguide_nodes 0,1, bguide_cfg -1 (so CFG 5), ctx 0, policy never is indeed a target-only T_{V={0,1}} sample (bg1_n01_s4321 spec_v0.json).

GAP 1: a necessary assumption is missing, although A1-A6 are presented as the complete list. Lemma 1 needs the draft mean mD_t to be fixed by the true past alone: the true state plus keys < t, never current or future keys. A2 constrains only mT. With lookahead, discarded speculative forwards were built from epsD[t], epsD[t+1], and so on. Any side channel from them into a later mD or mT breaks the proposal law and lets the draft enter the output law. Possible channels: Fast KV slots or the scalar index tensors global_end_index/local_end_index, the Base KV cache, cached tensors. Within a chunk the Fast forward overwrites the current slot before attending (model_fast.py:148-162), so that path is safe. Across chunks, safety depends on how and when the restore is done (see Gap 2).

GAP 2 (concrete bias in the pseudocode as written, L >= 1). In step 3, advance_commit(out, t, pref) runs INSIDE the coupling loop and evaluates X_c = g(z_{c,3}) plus the Fast KV commit. restore_fastKV_to(pref) runs only AFTER the loop. Cache size: the Fast KV cache holds 18 latent frames INCLUDING the 6 sinks (binding_v2.py:168-170 kv_size = frame_seqlen*local_attn; spec_v0.py:21 and :64 --fast-win 18). Mechanism, with L >= 1 and the frontier at (c,2), c >= 5: 1) the draft phase runs the chunk-(c+1) node-0 Fast forward; 2) that forward ROLLS the cache and evicts 3 non-sink frames (model_fast.py:133-149); 3) the node-2 whole-state test almost surely rejects (acceptance about 1e-573); 4) g(reflected z_{c,3}) is then computed on the rolled cache, with 3 fewer context frames than T_H's g. Example: chunk 5 loses latent frames 6-8. Result: X_c differs from T_H's g for chunks 5-11, i.e. 7 of the 12 Base-owned chunks, in essentially every such round. The Fast rollout depth then influences the output law. Second path: if the 'real commit' also recomputes g for an ACCEPTED z_{c,3}, X_c^real differs from X_c^spec, while mT for chunk c+1 was already computed with X_c^spec. That violates A2's 'bit for bit'. This contradicts the claim 'for any L >= 0' and A4.

GAP 3 (variant 3 T_H-KV is not 'same algorithm and proof'). kv_sync (spec_v0.py:339-351) detects prefix changes only by chunk COUNT: it resets only if nc < KVS['n']. Failure sequence: 1) with L >= 1 the Base KV absorbs the speculative X_c^spec; 2) a node-2 rejection produces X_c^real with the same count; 3) the next round's kv_x0 for chunk c+1 attends to the stale X_c^spec. X_c^spec is a function of epsD[(c,2)] and Fast, so A2 fails and the result is biased. The same problem applies to each of the W per-GPU worker caches. L=0 is fine because commits there are in-order appends.

GAP 4: A5 is incomplete. Several flags silently change g, the prefix or the target, beyond --bguide, --hint-lora and --plan-video: --histguide changes fast_x0 and hence g (spec_v0.py:413-427); --fast-lora merges into the Fast weights, changing g; --tex-lora (TX); --kv-mem/--kv-low (KVM); --fast-win changes g's window; --noise-corr gives AR(1)-correlated eps_{c,0}, violating the stated iid N(0,I); --chunk0-from; --seam re-commits a modified previous chunk (spec_v0.py:811); --polish; --bguide-cfg, which base_x0_at also uses for the SPECSTEP target CFG (spec_v0.py:332), so a leftover value silently changes T; --ctx/--guide/--nodes/--spec-nodes/--start; the env var SPECWM_SKIP_COMMIT (binding_v2.commit). A worker OOM or exception must abort the run, not fall back to the draft. spec_v0.py:58 notes 480p OOM with both experts resident at late chunks.

GAP 5 (minor, precision). A2's 'the realised evaluation is the kernel draw' makes the target kernel depend on GPU and scheduling nondeterminism. Exactness, and 'equal in law' with the spec-null arm, hold only up to floating point. State that explicitly, and give the pathwise check a tolerance.

GAP 6 (minor, keys). hash(seed, c, k, purpose) must be a deterministic hash. Python's hash() of a str is salted per process, so the W Base worker processes would draw different zeta for the same key. That is not biased, because fresh draws are still valid. It does break Corollary (i)'s common-random-numbers null, reproducibility, and the pathwise identity test.

DOC/EVIDENCE ERRORS (not bias). (a) Fast cache: '6 sink + 18 window' is wrong. It is 18 frames including 6 sinks, and g's window should be written that way in T_H. (b) The jar 9999 freeze of bg1_n01 is UNVERIFIED in the logs: NIGHT3_NOTES.md:155 reports only castle 4321. bg1_n0123 was killed (same line), so there is no target-only sample with node 2 or 3 Base-owned. 'T_{0,1,2} at least as mean-seeking' is a conjecture. (c) E[progress] should be sum_j prod_{i<j} a_i. As written, prod_{i<=j} gives about 0, not 1. (d) The gap between measured and theoretical acceptance reaches 0.07 (castle node 0: 0.55 vs 0.48), not 0.02-0.05. (e) The flicker coupling-inequality argument compares Fast-only with Base-70, but the relevant TV is against T_H, so the evidence is indirect. The probe KL was measured on Fast-only-prefix states, not on the T_H path. That is fine for orders of magnitude. (f) Literature. Soen et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13426: verified Table 3, ImageNet LDM, 1.22+-0.07 at K=50 and 2.25+-0.11 at K=250. The K proportional to sqrt(d) extrapolation is the design's own, not the paper's: UNVERIFIED heuristic. The paper's BLOCK verification, which 'provably improves the acceptance rate' over greedy per-transition verification, is an exact alternative the design omits. It should be cited, though it cannot rescue acceptance of about 1e-138. De Bortoli et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.05370: title, authors and exactness claim verified; the 'Alg. 4' numbering is UNVERIFIED. For the standard reflection-maximal coupling see Jacob, O'Leary, Atchade, https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.03625, and Bou-Rabee, Eberle, Zimmer, https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.00452.
