The ~600 s figure (related_work.md:11, '~10 min') cannot be right: 70 steps x 2 CFG forwards x ~19 s per 41-latent (63k-token) forward, from a quadratic fit to the 3.74 s / 7.53 s profile, gives about 2,660 s. Consequences: T_H alone (~740 s, modelled) is about 3.8x faster than Base-70, the running ctx-9 specstep (349 s) is about 8x faster, and plan->render (114-206 s) is 14-25x faster, not 3-5x. All of these gains come from the target definition, not from speculation.

THE DEFAULT TARGET T_H (ctx 0, 'what the current code samples') IS NOT WHAT THE QUEUE SAMPLES. scripts/q173_bundles.sh:156 launches specstep with --resident --ctx 9. The ctx-0 resident attempt ran out of GPU memory on the Base GPU at 94.35 of 94.97 GiB (exp/queue/w23_night.log, s4321, 4:47-5:01 AM CDT; the s1234 attempt failed on GPU contention). ctx 9 changes the law: the window is the last 9 prefix latents, the conditioning image is decoded latent j, and poses are offset by 4j (spec_v0.py:194-201 and 331). Consequences: the null batch and every 'exact w.r.t. T' statement must refer to T_{ctx9}. The 17-18 s per call applies only to ctx 0; at ctx 9 a CFG call costs about 7.5 s (t_spec 24.1 s per chunk for 3 calls).

THE 0.94x SEQUENTIAL FIGURE DEPENDS ON THE CONFIGURATION. At ctx 0 the per-chunk ratio runs from 0.75x (chunk 1, 3.4 s per CFG call) to 0.96x (chunk 12, 35 s per call), about 0.93x over the whole clip. At the running ctx 9 (t_B about 7.5-8 s) it is 0.86-0.94x. Fast-only runs take 61-72 s for 65 forwards including decode, so t_F is at most about 1.0 s, not 1.4 s.

THE T_H-KV SPEED (3.5-3.9 s per CFG call, and the 210 s end of 210-570 s) WAS MEASURED AT kv_win=6. NIGHT2_NOTES.md:32 and :36 report 'kv (CFG, cached) ~3.5 s ... with 1.5 s + sink memory', i.e. the cache holds the chunk-0 sink (3 latents) plus the last 6 latents. A clean full-prefix KV cache at chunk 12 would be 36 latents x 1,537 tokens x 40 layers x 2 x 5,120 x 2 B, about 45 GB per text context or about 91 GB with CFG. That cannot sit next to a 28 GB expert on a 95 GB GPU. So T_H-KV also drops most of the prefix, a change the design does not mention. NIGHT3 lines 13-18 and 62-65 show that dropping the prefix moves Base as far as a new seed (jar c10: 0.94 vs a seed floor of 0.83) and causes material and scene swaps. KV-reuse RePaint also drifted (NIGHT3:5, white liquid).

THE 210 s FIGURE NEEDS EVERY FREE GPU. The node-0 precompute stream costs sum_c 2*t_fwd(3c+3), about 212 s of GPU time plus about 50 s of conditioning and VAE work. With one spare high-expert GPU that stream becomes the bottleneck (about 225-270 s wall, modelled); with two spare GPUs it is about 160 s. So 210 s uses all of GPUs 4-7 (Fast, Base-low, and 2x Base-high) and leaves nothing for the concurrent null batch. T_H' without KV works with one spare GPU, and its critical path is about 530 s (modelled 743 -> 531 s, -29%, consistent with the design's '~1/3').

SELF-DRAFTING: CITATION VERIFIED, EXTRAPOLATION NOT. Soen et al. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13426, Table 3: ImageNet LDM, latent 64x64x3 = 12,288 dims, eps=0.5, gamma=7) report 1.22x at K=50 and 2.25x at K=250, as wall-clock against DDPM. The sqrt(d) scaling is the design's own heuristic; the paper does not discuss how acceptance scales with d (UNVERIFIED). A stronger objection: those wall-clock gains need the gamma drafted states verified in parallel at almost no extra cost. Our Base forwards are compute-bound (18-63k tokens) and batched forwards fail, so each verification needs its own GPU and full forward. That caps gamma at 3 on GPUs 4-7 and saves no FLOPs. Also, for the literal Base-70 whole-clip chain d is about 4.0M (16x41x58x106), not 295k, which gives K of about 900 for 1.22x. The net-loss verdict holds, and more strongly than the design argues.

THE L=1 BREAK-EVEN IS DERIVED WRONGLY. With the frontier target running concurrently and the second target dispatched at 2*t_F, E[round time] = t_B + 2a*t_F and E[progress] = 1 + a. The speed-up is therefore > 1 exactly when t_B > 2*t_F, for any a > 0, and the gain is about a*(1 - 2*t_F/t_B). The design's condition 'a >= t_F/t_B' (a >= 0.077 / 0.38) is the wrong criterion. This does not change any number, because a <= 1e-53.

THE 'MODEL-FREE' COUPLING-INEQUALITY ARGUMENT IS MISAPPLIED. It needs the TV distance between Fast's and T's per-chunk kernels given the same prefix. Clip-level flicker of Fast-only vs Base-70 (n = 3 each) compares different objects: T_H is not Base-70, and clip marginals are not per-chunk conditionals. It does not bound acceptance; the Gaussian computation alone makes the point.

SMALL NUMERIC ERRORS. Castle node-0 token acceptance is 0.548 measured vs 0.485 in theory, a gap of 0.063, outside the stated 0.02-0.05. The median/mean ratio of lr is 0.71-0.91, not 0.85-0.95. The rel-x0 per-chunk ranges are 97-480% / 36-67% / 28-48% (the design quotes task means). The claim that bg1_n01 froze on jar 9999 is not recorded: NIGHT3 documents only the castle 4321 full run (12:05 AM) and a smoke, and no temporal_eval exists for jar 9999 bg1_n01 (UNVERIFIED).

RUNNING W > 1 PARALLEL BASE WORKERS IS HARD AND BUYS NOTHING. Each parallel Base worker must be its own process because batched forwards fail. ctx-0 windows need expert swapping, since both experts resident runs out of GPU memory (the probe runs swapped: peak 63.9 GB, 23 swaps, ~15 s). Host RAM already ran out at 6 Base processes (NIGHT3:175, 774 GB). So W <= 3 on GPUs 4-7. The L>0 machinery (speculative Fast commits, snapshot and restore of the ~21 GiB Fast KV cache, cross-chunk Base evaluations) is moderate-to-high effort for zero expected gain and should not be built.

MISSED SPEED LEVER (not a refutation). Running the CFG cond and uncond forwards on two GPUs halves every critical-path Base call without any batching. I estimate T_H' at about 320 s and T_{ctx9} at about 200-210 s (UNVERIFIED in code; it needs a third expert copy).
verdicts.suggested_fix:
1. Keep the no-go verdict for exact speculation at chunk dimensionality. Add the ctx-9 specstep data point: acceptance is still <= 1e-53 per chunk.
2. Correct the Base-70 time to ~2,800 s (2,737-3,110 s over 43 runs) everywhere, and restate every speed ratio against it. Say explicitly that any speed-up comes from the target definition.
3. Define the default target as the one the queue actually samples: T_{ctx9}, --resident, window conditioned on decoded latent j with poses offset by 4j. The alternative is to run ctx 0 without --resident (expert swaps, ~64 GB peak) and make the null batch use exactly the same flags.
4. Describe T_H-KV as a truncated-context target (kv_win=6: sink plus 6 latents) and give the reason: a full-prefix CFG KV cache needs ~91 GB. Give the GPU count behind 210 s (4 GPUs: Fast, Base-low, 2x Base-high); with one spare high-expert GPU it is ~225-270 s.
5. Replace the L=1 break-even with the condition t_B > 2*t_F and the gain a*(1-2*t_F/t_B). Drop the flicker-based TV argument, or label it illustrative.
6. For self-drafting, mark the sqrt(d) scaling UNVERIFIED. Add the stronger objection: parallel verification is compute-bound here and batching fails, so gamma <= GPUs and no FLOPs are saved.
7. Implementation: do not build L>0. Make L=0 concurrent: launch Base base_x0_at on a thread before Fast's fast_x0, and key the two global-RNG draws (torch.randn_like in base_x0_at and torch.rand_like in the accept test) for reproducibility. Run the same-flag target-only null batch.
8. If speed is wanted inside the exact framework, the cheap levers are CFG cond/uncond split across two GPUs and T_H' node-0 precompute. Both change wall-clock, not the law, apart from T_H's 2e-4 prefix term, which bf16 rounding hides.

design.name: SpecAR-PR: an exact chunk-level AR speculative sampler. Fast drafts, per-position reflection coupling, the tail after the last Fast node belongs to Base, and the Base target is anchored to a Base low-res plan (strict-AR variant: --spec-init noise)
design.summary:
This is the smallest change to the existing `--specstep` that makes the claim "unbiased w.r.t. Base" true and worth testing, plus a one-day experiment that follows the professor's item-4 protocol.

The five code changes (all in /home/hk28965/specwm/lingbot-world-v2/specwm/spec_v0.py):
- (1) After the last coupled Fast node, the chunk is finished by a Base-only tail. Today Fast's deterministic node-3 x0 is committed, which puts Fast into the output law (audit bug HIGH-1).
- (2) Chunk 0 goes through the same process. This needs an empty-prefix branch in base_x0_at.
- (3) All randomness gets seeded generators: the init noise xi, the RePaint prefix noise zeta, and the acceptance uniforms u. Right now zeta and u come from unseeded global CUDA RNGs, so seeds are not i.i.d.
- (4) The target is defined by its own flags (--spec-cfg, --spec-target rp|kv, --spec-init plan|noise), and `pol==never` is asserted.
- (5) Primary target: the chunk state at Fast node 1 (sigma 0.937) is initialised from the Base low-res whole-clip plan, re-noised: z1 = 0.063*P_c + 0.937*xi. Base's layout step then comes from Base's own whole-clip sample, not from chunk-wise RePaint from noise, which is known to snap back to frame 0 and ignore the camera (NIGHT3_NOTES 18:40 and 22:40, 9/24). All target calls then use the low expert (t <= 937 < 947), so neither --resident nor expert swaps are needed.

What the output law is:
- The output is distributed exactly as T_PR = Base plan x Base chunk-AR render. Fast (plus its plan-hint LoRA) only decides which latent positions of the intermediate states are copied from the draft.
- Exactness is proved per transition (De Bortoli et al. 2025, Alg. 4 / Prop 3.1, https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.05370) and verified in every run by free calibration statistics.

What it cannot do:
- It cannot be faster than running T_PR alone. Every accepted state still needs its Base forward; the only possible speed gain is verifying several drafted transitions in parallel, and that requires the whole chunk state to be accepted.
- From our own logged Fast-vs-Base probes (q156 runs, 9/22), whole-chunk acceptance is below 1e-58 at every node. Per-position acceptance is 0.53-0.90.
- Expected speed-up vs the target alone: 0.83-0.97x. The theoretical ceiling, even with a perfect drafter and a spare Base GPU, is 1.33x for this schedule.
- Speed therefore has to come from the target's design (plan anchoring, KV cache, CFG truncation): T_PR takes about 245-560 s vs Base-70 at about 600 s. Or it comes from biased shortcuts (v2 plan->render, 206 s), whose bias this experiment measures directly against their own exact target.

Experiment:
- 8 seeds x 2 failure prompts. Arms: A = exact spec, B = target-only (the null; must match A in law), C = Fast-only, D = Base-70 batch, E = v2 render on the same plans.
- drift_rate2.py for no-drift rates with Wilson CIs, McNemar A-vs-B paired by seed, in-run calibration z-scores, and watching the videos.
- About 4 h of coding, a 45 min smoke, and 2-4 h of batch on two GPU pairs.
design.target_definition:
What "unbiased" can mean here. Base (LingBot-World v1 base-cam = Wan2.2 I2V A14B + camera) is a bidirectional whole-clip model. It does not provide the conditionals p_B(X_c | X_<c) of its 161-frame joint law, so no AR sampler can be exact w.r.t. the Base-70 joint distribution. Exactness is always w.r.t. an explicitly defined Base-only AR process T. How close T is to Base-70 is an empirical question, answered by the drift protocol (arm B vs arm D).

PRIMARY TARGET T_PR (--spec-init plan): a hierarchical Base process.
- (a) Plan. P ~ Base whole-clip sampler at 576x304: plan_gen `cr` = 16-step UniPC, CFG 5 on the first 6 steps, flow reuse 9/11/13, seed = clip seed (133 s; l4c = 66 s is an alternative, but then the target changes). U(P) = VAE-encode(cubic-upscale(decode(P))) to the 480p latent grid (the existing `--plan-video` 'pix' path, PLAN['lat'] in draft_chunk). U(P)_c is chunk c's 3 latent frames.
- (b) Chunk-AR render, c = 0..12 (N = 13 chunks, 39 latents, 153 frames), given the committed X_<c. Grid: Fast node sigmas s = (0.99980, 0.93727, 0.83306, 0.62469) (binding_v2 shift-5 idx 0/250/500/750).
  - z1 = (1 - s1)*U(P)_c + s1*xi_c, with xi_c ~ N(0, I). xi is the existing chunk_noise(ci, g) draw.
  - Two stochastic transitions k = 1->2 and 2->3: z_{k+1} ~ N(m_T(z_k), std_k^2 I).
    - renoise kernel (default; Fast's native): m_T = (1 - s')*x0_B, std = s'.
    - ddpm kernel (optional, better suited to an undistilled target): r = ((1-s)s')/((1-s')s) = 0.334 at both steps; m_T = (1-s')(1-r^2)*x0_B + (r s'/s) z; std = s'*sqrt(1 - r^2).
  - x0_B = Base low expert at t = 1000*s, cond-only (--spec-cfg 1, consistent with the validated cfg6 truncation: CFG is only ever applied at t >= 943). Two variants:
    - rp: base_x0_at, a RePaint window [ (1-s)*X_<c[j:] + s*zeta, z ] with --ctx 9 (the window image is decoded latent j, poses offset 4j). Use ctx 0 for the full prefix and start image.
    - kv: kv_x0, block-causal Base whose clean-prefix KV cache holds sink + kv_win latents.
    - zeta ~ N(0, I) is fresh per call and seeded.
  - Tail (Base only, deterministic given its zeta draws): Euler on the Base velocity v = (z - x0_B(z, sigma))/sigma, from s3 = 0.6247 to 0. The n_tail = 6 sigmas are Base's own shift-10 spacing, sigma_ref(u) = 10u/(1+9u), u = 0.1428*(1 - j/6). Output X_c = z at sigma 0.
  - Commit X_c. This is Fast's KV commit, used only for drafting, plus the Base KV write in the kv variant.
- Law: T_PR(P, X) = p_plan(P) * prod_c ∫ N(xi) N(zeta) K_{1->2} K_{2->3} delta(X_c - Tail(z3; X_<c, zeta_tail)).
- Fast does not appear anywhere in T_PR. The high expert is never used, since every target call has t <= 937.3 < 947 (wan_i2v_A14B.py boundary 0.947).

STRICT-AR VARIANT T_AR (--spec-init noise): for a professor who wants no global plan.
- z0 ~ N(0, I) at s0 = 0.9998. Three stochastic transitions 0->1, 1->2, 2->3. Node 0 uses the high expert with CFG 5; the rest are as above. Same tail.
- This is exactly the chunk-wise Base-RePaint-from-noise process whose snap-back and camera-ignoring failures are documented (NIGHT3 9/24 18:40 and 22:40). Its drift rate should be measured, but it is not expected to be a good target.

EXPLICIT NON-CLAIMS:
- Not exact w.r.t. Base-70. Not exact w.r.t. Base-at-480p-whole-clip.
- With --spec-tail 0 (legacy), the law is the hybrid H: node 3 is Fast. Report that as exact w.r.t. H only.
- Exactness is w.r.t. the computed bf16 Base function and PyTorch's pseudo-random streams.
design.algorithm_pseudocode:
Constants: s = [0.99980, 0.93727, 0.83306, 0.62469]; CS = 3; N = 13; positions per chunk = 3*58*106 = 18,444, each a 16-vector (d = 295,104).
Generators: Gxi = the existing CPU stream g (chunk_noise); Geps = g (the draft noise; shared by arms A and B, so both see common random numbers); Gu(seed, c, j) on dev0; Gz(seed, c, j | 'tail', i) on dev1.

```
BaseX0(z, sigma, X_<c, key):   # the target's only model call
    t = 1000*sigma; expert = high if t >= 947 else low; g = 5 if expert == high else spec_cfg (1)
    rp: zeta ~ N(0,I) from Gz(key)
        lat = cat[(1-sigma)*X_<c[j:] + sigma*zeta, z]
        x0 = (lat - sigma*BaseFlow(lat, t, cond(F, j), g))[chunk slots]
    kv: kv_sync(X_<c)   # clean t=0 prefix KV
        x0 = z - sigma*BaseKV.forward(z, t, y_c, cam_c)
    return x0 (fp32)

kernel(x0, z, s, s'):
    renoise: return ((1-s')*x0, s')
    ddpm:    r = ((1-s)*s')/((1-s')*s)
             return ((1-s')*(1-r*r)*x0 + (r*s'/s)*z, s'*sqrt(1-r*r))

SPEC_AR(seed, arm in {A, B}, init in {plan, noise}):
  X = []; Fast.reset(); Pl = VAE(cubic_up(plan video))   # PLAN['lat'], 480p latents
  for c in 0..N-1:
    xi = chunk_noise(c, g)
    if init == plan: z = (1-s[1])*Pl[:, 3c:3c+3] + s[1]*xi; K = [1, 2, 3]
    else:            z = xi;                                 K = [0, 1, 2, 3]
    for j in 0..len(K)-2:                                    # stochastic transitions K[j] -> K[j+1]
      sg, sg2 = s[K[j]], s[K[j+1]]
      in parallel:  x0T = BaseX0(z, sg, X, (c, j))                               # dev1, thread
                    x0D = Fast.x0(z, K[j] | Fast KV(X), y_c with plan hint)       # dev0; skipped if arm == B
      (mT, sd) = kernel(x0T, z, sg, sg2)
      eps ~ N(0, I) from g                                   # same draw in A and B
      if arm == B: z = mT + sd*eps; log calib; continue
      (mD, _) = kernel(x0D, z, sg, sg2); zd = mD + sd*eps     # draft sample (Fast's own transition)
      for every position p (vectorised over [1,3,58,106]):
        D_p   = (mD_p - mT_p)/sd                             # 16-vector
        logr_p = -D_p.eps_p - |D_p|^2/2                      # = log N(zd_p; mT_p, sd^2) - log N(zd_p; mD_p, sd^2)
        u_p ~ U(0,1) from Gu(seed, c, j)
        if log u_p <= min(0, logr_p): z_p = zd_p             # keep the draft
        else: e_p = D_p/|D_p|; z_p = mT_p + sd*(eps_p - 2(e_p.eps_p)e_p)   # reflect; no extra target call
      log: acc = mean(accept); acc_pred = mean(2*Phi(-|D_p|/2)); dmean = mean|D_p|
           log10 alpha_chunk = log10(2) + log_ndtr(-|D|/2)/ln10
           calibration: r = (z - mT)/sd -> z_mean = mean(r)*sqrt(d), z_var = (var(r) - 1)*sqrt(d/2),
                        z_proj = mean_p(e_p.r_p)*sqrt(n_p) over |D_p| > 0.05,
                        z_acc = (sum acc - sum a_p)/sqrt(sum a_p(1 - a_p))
    # target-owned finish (no draft)
    sig_tail = [sigma_ref(0.1428*(1 - i/6)) for i in 0..6]   # 0.6247 -> 0, Base shift-10 spacing
    for i in 0..5:
      x0 = BaseX0(z, sig_tail[i], X, ('tail', c, i))
      z  = z + (sig_tail[i+1] - sig_tail[i])*(z - x0)/sig_tail[i]
    X_c = z
    Fast.commit(X_c)   # draft conditioning only
    [kv: BaseKV.write(X_c, t=0)]
    X.append(X_c)
  return VAE.decode(cat X)
```

Calls per chunk:
- T_PR: 2 coupled Base calls + 6 tail Base calls. Arm A adds 2 Fast calls (in parallel with Base) and 1 Fast commit.
- T_AR: +1 coupled transition at node 0 (high expert, CFG 2 passes; 2 expert swaps per chunk unless ctx 9 + resident fits).

One-step lookahead is not implemented. It would verify the next transition on a spare Base GPU from the draft state zd, and pays only when the whole chunk is accepted (probability alpha_chunk). Only its alpha is logged, to document why it is not worth building.
design.unbiasedness_proof:
Notation:
- F_{c,j} is the history before transition j of chunk c: P, X_<c, xi_c, the states z_{c,<=j}, all zeta used so far, and all previous eps and u.
- Target transition: Q = N(mT, sd^2 I). Draft: Pd = N(mD, sd^2 I).

Assumptions (each one is a code requirement):
- A1 (same Gaussian family). mT, mD and sd are F_{c,j}-measurable, meaning they are computed before this step's eps and u are drawn. sd is the same scalar for draft and target, which holds because both use the same (s, s') and the same kernel type. The ddpm kernel's b*z term is also shared.
- A2 (fresh randomness). eps ~ N(0, I_d) and u ~ U[0,1]^18444 are independent of each other and of F_{c,j}. In code: eps is one draw from the CPU stream g; u comes from a dedicated seeded generator; neither is reused and neither is drawn before mT and mD exist. Use eps directly; do not recover it as (z - mD)/s' (the current code does, with only ~1e-7 fp32 error, but using eps removes the question).
- A3 (the target is the target). mT is produced by exactly the computation that defines T: the same weights, conditioning (y, poses, empty prompt, ctx window), CFG rule, expert rule, and prefix-noise law zeta ~ N(0, I) independent of eps and u. It is computed once, and that one value is used both in log r and in the reflection. bf16 nondeterminism only redefines the target function; it does not break the argument.
- A4 (no adaptivity through the target). After each coupling, everything that affects X depends on the draft only through the coupled state z: the tail, the commit, and later target calls. So: no retries, no fallbacks, no switching policy or schedule on acceptance, and policy == never (assert that bguide, polish, seam, handoff, corr-* and sem/verify policies are off). The Base conditioning must not see the hint: base_cond comes from b1.prepare, which is separate from Fast's y, whose in-place hint is restored before commit; the audit verified this.
- A5 (the other target components are sampled as in T). xi and zeta ~ N(0, I) come from their own streams. P is produced by the stated plan sampler with the clip seed. The tail is a deterministic function of (z3, X_<c, zeta_tail).
- A6 (the draft is arbitrary). mD may depend on anything in F_{c,j}: Fast's KV cache (which contains the Base-produced X_<c), the LoRA, the plan hint, past acceptance outcomes. No property of Fast is assumed.

Lemma 1 (one position, one transition; reflection maximal coupling, De Bortoli et al. 2025 Prop 3.1, https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.05370; after Bou-Rabee et al. 2020, attribution as given by the literature agent).
- Work in units of sd. Rotate so that e = D/|D| is the first axis. The 15 orthogonal coordinates of the draft sample and of the reflected sample are both mT_perp + eps_perp, and mD_perp = mT_perp, so they are already target-distributed and untouched. That leaves a 1-D problem: draft N(delta, 1) with delta = |D|, target N(0, 1), Z = delta + eps1.
- Accepted density at y: phi(y - delta) * min(1, phi(y)/phi(y - delta)) = min(phi(y), phi(y - delta)).
- On rejection the output is -eps1. Its density at y is phi(y) * [1 - min(1, phi(y - delta)/phi(y))] = phi(y) - min(phi(y), phi(y - delta)).
- The two add to phi(y). So the output is N(mT, sd^2 I_16), and P(output = draft) = 1 - TV = 2*Phi(-|D|/2), which is the maximum possible. If D = 0 the draft is always kept, and it is target-distributed.

Lemma 2 (factorisation). Given F_{c,j}, Q and Pd factorise over the 18,444 positions: N(m, sd^2 I_d) = prod_p N(m_p, sd^2 I_16). Base's x0 depends on the whole previous state, but that is irrelevant, because m_p is fixed given F. The pairs (eps_p, u_p) are independent across p, so the per-position outputs are conditionally independent and each is N(mT_p, sd^2 I_16) by Lemma 1. Their product is Q, and the transition is exact.

Theorem (induction over (c, j)). Assume A1-A6. Suppose the law of (P, X_<c, z_{c,<=j}, zeta so far) under the algorithm equals its law under T. By Lemma 2, z_{c,j+1} given the history has law Q, which is T's kernel. The chunk init (xi) and the tail/commit are the target's own maps of target-distributed inputs plus fresh target noise. Chunk 0 is included because base_x0_at gets an empty-prefix branch. By induction the output X has law T_PR, or T_AR with --spec-init noise.

Corollaries:
- (i) Null equality: the output has the same law as arm B (z_{k+1} = mT + sd*eps, no draft). So the item-4 drift rates of A and B must agree. A significant difference is an implementation bug, not a finding.
- (ii) In-run checks: r = (z_{k+1} - mT)/sd ~ N(0, I_d), and e_p.r_p ~ N(0, 1) for any past-measurable e. The legacy biased rule (redraw from the target on rejection) and accept-all both give E[e.r] > 0, so z_proj detects them. The empirical acceptance must match sum_p 2*Phi(-|D_p|/2), which z_acc checks.
- (iii) Fast influences only which intermediate positions are reused. X_c is always the output of the Base tail.

What breaks it (a checklist for review):
- Fast's final x0 committed (today's code).
- Chunk 0 skipped.
- u or zeta drawn from the unseeded global CUDA RNG. The law is still exact per run, but seeds are not i.i.d.
- --bguide or --hint without a plan feeding Base.
- A non-'never' policy (base_repaint_chunk replacement).
- The legacy --policy spec.
- Computing mT twice (a different zeta for the ratio than for the reflection).
- Drawing eps before x0D (fine) versus making x0D depend on eps (not fine).
design.acceptance_analysis:
Formulas:
- Per position p (16 dims): a_p = 2*Phi(-|D_p|/2).
- Whole chunk (18,444 positions, d = 295,104): alpha = 2*Phi(-|D|/2), with |D|^2 = sum_p |D_p|^2.

design.expected_speedup:
Short answer: at most 1.0x vs running the same target alone; expect 0.83-0.97x. That is structural. Exact speculative sampling needs the target's mean at every state it keeps. The only gain is parallel verification of a lookahead window, which requires whole-state acceptance (alpha < 1e-58 here). Diffusion forwards are compute-bound: Base window cost is linear in tokens, about 0.2 ms/token (3.74 s at 18.4k tokens, 7.53 s at 32.3k), so batching on one GPU is not free either.

Per-clip render cost. Estimates are built from measured per-forward costs:
- rp, cond-only, full prefix: 1.7 s (6 latents) to 9.0 s (24 latents), probe2 log 9/22.
- rp with --ctx 9, cond-only: 3.7-3.8 s.
- kv (kvg1, sink + 6 latents): 0.85-0.88 s (NIGHT2_NOTES).
- Fast: about 1.4 s per forward; Fast render 73 s.
- Plan: cr 133 s, l4c 66 s.
- Model loading, about 3-6 min per process, is excluded (UNVERIFIED).

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B target-only, rp ctx0 | 8 | ~815 | ~950 | 1.00x | 0.63x |
| B target-only, rp ctx9 | 8 | ~370 | ~500 | 1.00x | 1.2x |
| A spec exact, rp ctx9, sequential | 8 + 3 Fast | ~425 | ~560 | 0.87x | 1.07x |
| A spec exact, rp ctx9, Fast in a parallel thread | 8 (+commit) | ~385 | ~520 | ~0.96x | 1.15x |
| B target-only, kv | 8 + 1 write | ~110 | ~245 | 1.00x | 2.4x |
| A spec exact, kv, parallel (Fast 1.4 s > Base 0.9 s is the bottleneck) | 9 | ~130 | ~265 | ~0.83x | 2.3x |
| E v2 plan->Fast render (BIASED; draft only) | 0 | 73 | 206 | - | 2.9x |

Ceilings:
- (a) With the measured kernels, one-step lookahead on a spare Base GPU gives 1 + O(alpha) = 1.00x.
- (b) Even a perfect drafter (alpha = 1) saves at most the 2 coupled passes of the 8 per chunk, because the 6-step tail is target-only: 8/6 = 1.33x.
- (c) alpha = 0.87 would need a_p >= 0.999 (x0 within about 0.1-0.4% RMS): 1.28x. alpha = 0.5: 1.14x.

T_AR (strict AR) adds one high-expert CFG transition plus 2 expert swaps per chunk: about 560 s rp-ctx9 target-only. Same <= 1x conclusion.

Where speed can actually come from (not speculation):
- The design of the target: plan anchoring skips the high expert and the layout steps; KV caching is about 4x cheaper per pass than ctx9 RePaint; cond-only in the low-noise regime halves cost.
- Pipelining a lagged-prefix target on 2 GPUs (up to 2x; a different target, not speculative).
- Biased shortcuts (v2 render, hybrid H_m = the target owns only the first m transitions, SDVG-style reward gates https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.17397, De Bortoli's tau>1 tempering). Their bias is measurable as drift(E or H_m) - drift(B) on the same plans.

The quantitative statement for the professor: with Fast as the drafter, exact speculative sampling reproduces the target at 0.83-1.0x of its cost. The trade-off to report is bias vs time between B (exact, about 245-500 s) and E (73 s render, bias = drift_E - drift_B).

design.risks:
1. Target quality is unknown, and it decides whether the result means anything. T_PR's render has 2 big stochastic steps (0.94 to 0.83 to 0.625) with an undistilled Base, whose x0 at s >= 0.83 is a posterior mean, followed by a 6-step Euler tail.
   - It may come out soft. The notes found that Base refines of plans are softer than Base-70 (plan5).
   - It may show seams or colour re-anchoring with ctx 9, where the window image is a decoded prefix frame (colour drift was seen with al_ctx18).
   - Mitigation: the smoke by eye, the ddpm kernel, n_tail 8, or ctx 0 (about 2x cost).
   If B looks worse than E, the exact sampler is faithful to a poor target. Report that honestly rather than tuning the draft.
2. The KV variant is off-distribution. A clean t=0 prefix with block-causal attention was never trained. Block-causal RePaint from noise drifted, and the clean prefix broke the high expert. The low expert on a plan-anchored state has not been tested (UNVERIFIED). Use kv only if the smoke video is clean.
3. Strict-AR objection: T_PR contains a whole-clip plan, so it is not purely AR, and it needs the whole camera path up front (true in this benchmark). T_AR answers the literal request but inherits snap-back and camera-ignoring behaviour, and costs about 560 s per clip.
4. No speed-up (by construction). Do not let the write-up imply one. Speed numbers must be the target's own (plan anchoring, KV, CFG truncation), and biased methods' gains must be reported with their measured bias vs B.
5. Implementation traps that silently break exactness:
   - eps drawn twice, or a shifted RNG stream between the ratio and the reflection;
   - mT recomputed with a different zeta;
   - the hint y left in place during Base calls or the commit (currently restored, l.495);
   - legacy paths (--bguide, the hint without --plan-video, which calls base_x0_at at s = 1, and non-'never' policies);
   - torch.where broadcast shapes;
   - fp32 vs bf16 mixing in log r (compute in fp32 from the same tensors);
   - |D| = 0 (e = 0, always accept; already handled).
   The z_proj/z_acc/z_var checks catch most of these, and the CPU unit test should cover both kernels.
6. RNG. The global CUDA streams are unseeded today (possibly identical across seeds; UNVERIFIED). Without the seeded generators, the 8 seeds are not i.i.d. and the item-4 comparison is weakened.
7. Resources.
   - Do not use --resident: both experts plus a 60k-token window is about 90 GB (audit). T_PR needs only the low expert.
   - Tonight's specstep smoke OOMed at prepare because of a co-tenant process on the same GPU. Keep GPUs exclusive.
   - Host RAM: each non-resident process pins about 56 GB of experts; at most 3 at once, with staggered starts.
   - Per-process loading of about 3-6 min dominates short runs (UNVERIFIED). An optional --seeds loop inside one process (b.reset_caches, KV.reset, cond_cache kept) would save about 1.5-2 h.
8. Statistics. n = 16 per arm gives low power for rate equality (about 0.75 power for a 0.5 gap; nothing for small gaps). A, B and E share the plan per seed, so drift status is largely inherited from P. That makes A vs B on drift weak, but the paired E-vs-B bias test sharp. Rely on the in-run calibration for exactness.
   - drift_rate2's threshold tau is the 95th percentile of leave-one-out over 8 Base seeds, effectively the maximum. Methods are compared against all 8 Base clips while Base leave-one-out uses 7, which slightly favours the methods.
   - Castle Base-70 currently has only 3 seeds done.
9. Window-end darkening (the reason --end-pad exists). Every RePaint window ends at the current chunk. Check the last frames of each chunk in the smoke; if they darken, add end-pad latents to the target window. That changes the target's definition but not exactness.

issues: VERDICT ON THE MATH: I could not refute it. Lemma 1 holds. In units of sd along e = D/|D|, the accepted density is phi(y-d)*min(1, phi(y)/phi(y-d)) = min(phi(y), phi(y-d)) and the rejected (reflected, -eps1) density is phi(y) - min(phi(y), phi(y-d)); they add up to phi(y). The 15 orthogonal coordinates are mT_perp + eps_perp in both branches, and P(keep) = 2*Phi(-|D|/2) = 1 - TV. Lemma 2 (factorisation given F) and the induction over (c, j) are also correct under A1-A6. The citation checks out: De Bortoli et al. 2025, Alg. 4 = reflection maximal coupling, Prop 3.1 = output ~ q with P(Y != Y~) = TV (https://arxiv.org/html/2501.05370); origin in Bou-Rabee et al. 2020 (https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.aoap/1596009621). What the proof shows is exactness w.r.t. T_PR. It is conditional on A1-A6, and several of those assumptions are not guaranteed by the implementation plan, as listed below.

CODE CHECKS THAT PASSED (spec_v0.py, base_cache.py, plan_kv.py): base_cond() builds Base conditioning only from b1.prepare(start image, or vae.decode of prefix latent j). It never reads Fast's b._y_chunks, so the plan hint cannot leak into the target. cond_cache is keyed (F, j, area), and within a run each key is first built from the committed prefix, so it is never stale when there is no rollback. BaseKV.forward writes the KV cache only when write=True (commit), so noisy target calls do not change later target calls. capture_base_kv removes its hooks. The expert boundary is 0.947*1000 = 947 > 937.27, so T_PR only ever uses the low expert. --spec-tries is dead code (only defined in argparse).

A2 HAZARD (generator keying, as written): the design names Gu(seed, c, j) on dev0 and Gz(seed, c, j) on dev1. If both are torch CUDA generators seeded with the same integer, they produce the same Philox stream on both devices. torch.rand(u) and torch.randn(zeta) would then be built from the same counter bits. Zeta enters mT, so u is no longer independent of (mT, logr), A2 fails, and exactness is lost. The bias is tiny, but the claim is exactness. The same risk applies to collisions with plan_gen's Philox seed (= clip seed) and with the legacy formulas seed*7919+ci, seed*31+ci, seed*17+ci*131+tries, seed*7+3. The spec must state domain-separated keys per role (u / zeta-coupled / zeta-tail / xi-eps / plan) and assert that no two generators share a seed.

CURRENT UNSEEDED RNG IS WORSE THAN 'NOT I.I.D.': I grep'd spec_v0.py, binding_v1/v2 and the wan I2V entry points and found no torch.manual_seed or torch.cuda.manual_seed. PyTorch's default generators start from a fixed constant (67280421310721), so the zeta stream (torch.randn_like on dev1) and the u stream (torch.rand_like on dev0) are probably identical across every run that has the same draw count. All 8 seeds x 2 prompts would share the same zeta and u. This is UNVERIFIED in-run, but it strengthens the case for fix (3).

A6 OVERCLAIM ('no property of Fast is assumed'): the coupler needs mD to be finite. If Fast returns NaN or Inf at a position, logr is NaN, the comparison is false, so it rejects; then e = dlt/dlt.norm().clamp_min(1e-12) is NaN and the output z is NaN. A single bad draft value poisons that position, and from there the target. Fix: for positions with non-finite D, output mT_p + sd*eps_p. That is still exactly N(mT_p, sd^2 I) because eps is independent.

SILENT FAST-LAW PATHS IN THE EXISTING CONTROL FLOW: `if a.specstep and ci >= a.start and outs and i in SPEC_NODES` (spec_v0.py:473) quietly keeps Fast's own sample z = (1-s)x0_D + s*eps whenever a transition is missing from --spec-nodes, the chunk is below --start (default 1), or outs is empty (chunk 0). A4's assert list must also require: SPEC_NODES == every stochastic transition in K; start == 0; and a per-chunk count that every stochastic transition went through the coupler. The target's CFG is also set by the wrong flag: base_x0_at uses `a.bguide_cfg if a.bguide_cfg > 0 else a.guide` (line 332), so --bguide-cfg would silently change the target. The following must be asserted off or pinned identically across arms, since each changes the computed target: --base-lora, --mixed-lora (these modify the live Base), --noise-corr (replaces xi ~ N(0, I) i.i.d. with an AR(1) noise field, which changes T), and the env vars SPECWM_PLUCKER_REF and SPECWM_NO_FLASH.

THE CALIBRATION STATISTICS CANNOT VERIFY A3-A5, so 'verified in every run' is an overclaim: r = (z - mT)/sd is computed with the same mT the code produced. If the target computation itself is wrong or draft-dependent (hint leak, wrong expert or CFG, altered prefix, stale conditioning, different numerics in arm A), z_mean, z_var, z_proj and z_acc all stay at N(0,1). They only test the coupler, and McNemar A-vs-B on 16 pairs has almost no power. Also, 416 is the count per statistic type; with 4 types there are 1664 tests, so the expected max |z| is about 3.5-3.6, not 3.3 (the 4.5 threshold is still fine).

'Fast only decides which positions are copied' is inaccurate. On rejection the output is mT + sd*refl_e(eps) with e = D/|D|, and e depends on mD. So Fast also sets the realised values at rejected positions. The law is unchanged, but A and B share far less than the CRN framing suggests, which weakens the paired test further.

TARGET-DEFINITION INCONSISTENCIES (no A-vs-B bias, but the T_PR/T_AR that gets computed is not the one written down): (a) the tail's first sigma is sigma_ref(0.1428) = 0.62489 (or 0.6250 for u = 1/7), not s3 = 0.62469, so Base is evaluated with a mislabelled sigma; set tail[0] := s3 exactly. (b) T_AR in the kv variant: KV = BaseKV(lambda: expert('low')) is hard-bound to the low expert, which contradicts 'node 0 uses the high expert with CFG 5'. (c) With ctx 9, the window's conditioning image is vae.decode of a 4-frame prefix latent read as a 1-frame image latent, and pose_offset is set via mutable b1._pose_offset. (d) U(P) passes through the lossy plan mp4 plus cv2 cubic resize, and that must be written into T. (e) The summary's phrase 'makes the claim unbiased w.r.t. Base true' is wrong. The plan sampler (16-step UniPC, CFG truncation, flow reuse), the RePaint conditioning and the 2 renoise + 6 Euler steps make T_PR a constructed process, not Base. The correct wording is 'exact w.r.t. T_PR'.

ROUNDING-LEVEL DEVIATIONS (negligible, but they will break a bitwise replay test unless handled): fp32 torch.rand has a 2^-24 grid and exp(logr) underflows below about -103, giving a deviation of at most about 6e-8 per position. base_cond's window-image VAE decode runs on dev0, which is Fast's GPU (Base thread, Fast's VAE). cuDNN algorithm choice or workspace fallback can then depend on free memory, which differs between arm A and arm B, so the 'computed bf16 target function' may differ between arms at the rounding level. Fix: do the decode on dev1 or precompute it, and set cudnn deterministic with benchmark off.

EXPERIMENT SELECTION/STOPPING: arm A uses more memory, so an OOM (e.g. during GPU takeovers) that leads to a dropped or re-run seed is differential attrition. Report all 16 seeds. A re-run must be a fully seeded replay (possible only after fix 3). The by-eye video judgement should be blinded to arm.

Bullo et al., speculative draft trees, exists (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17691), but its 'dimension warning' is UNVERIFIED because the abstract does not state it.

VERDICT: the design's main speed claim survives the arithmetic. The claim is that exact per-transition coupling gives at most 1.0x over running T_PR alone, with 0.83-0.97x expected. No parallel target evaluation is actually available: (a) Base's mean at transition j+1 depends on every position of the drafted state through bidirectional attention over [prefix, chunk], so lookahead needs whole-state acceptance; (b) chunk c+1's target calls need the exact Base-tail output X_c, so chunks cannot overlap; (c) batched Base forwards fail in the plucker path (onestep_profile_p9/p18.json record only B=1), so extra evaluations need extra GPUs, each holding a 28 GB expert. Several supporting numbers are wrong or overstated (below). None of them turns the result into a speedup.

ACCEPTANCE RECOMPUTED: renoise factors (1-s')/s' = 0.0669 / 0.2004 / 0.6008 and ddpm r = 0.334 / 0.3335 (factors 0.1889 / 0.5664) all check out. There are 18,444 positions (d = 295,104) and 4,611 tokens. For lookahead to reach alpha >= 0.5, |D| must be <= 1.349, i.e. RMS |D_p| <= 0.00993 and a_p >= 0.99604. That is correct. New data: tonight's per-position run specwm_out/spec_v0/sand_filling_up_jar/specstep_n012c9_never_s1234/spec_v0.json (Base CFG5, ctx9, Fast prefix) gives per-position acceptance 0.58-0.91 and mean |D_p| 0.227-1.382. By Jensen, the best chunk (c10, node 1, dmean 0.2266) gives alpha <= 10^-52.7 per chunk and <= 10^-18.2 per latent frame. So the claims 'alpha < 1e-58 in every measured case' and 'one latent frame < 1e-19' are both slightly false. The conclusion does not change.

WRONG BASELINE: 'Base-70 ~600 s' does not match this repo's measurements. Single-GPU gen_s in base70_s*/revisit.json is 2766-2793 s for castle and 2824-3111 s for jar (UniPC 70 steps, CFG 5/5, max_area 399360). NIGHT3_NOTES line 97 also says ~2800 s. A cost model fitted to the two measured forward times (t = 0.1618 n + 0.00221 n^2, n in thousands of tokens) predicts about 19 s per pass at 63k tokens, times 140 passes, which gives about 2660 s plus VAE. That agrees with the logs. So 'T_PR 245-560 s vs Base-70 600 s' understates T_PR's advantage about 5x. That advantage also comes entirely from redefining the target: 104 CFG-free calls on a 12-latent window, against Base-70's 140 CFG passes over the full 41 latents. None of it comes from speculation, and it should not be reported as a speculative speedup.

T_PR TIME: ctx 9 lands in the claimed range. ctx 0 does not. Fitted cost per CFG-free low-expert call: 3 latents 0.79 s, 6 latents 1.68 s, 9 latents 2.66 s, 12 latents 3.74 s, 39 latents 17.65 s. Per-chunk cond overhead is 2.7 s (t_cond 32.9 s over 12 chunks in the specstep run). With 8 Base calls per chunk and 13 chunks: rp ctx 9 = 375 s of Base, 441 s with the l4c plan, 508 s with the cr plan. rp ctx 0 (full prefix, which the design offers as an option) = 886 s of Base, 952-1019 s total, well outside '245-560 s'. kv = 109-131 s of Base, measured kvg1 at 0.85-0.88 s per call (NIGHT2 lines 32/36), 242-264 s with the cr plan. But the kv target is known to drift ('KV-reuse RePaint ... still drifts (white liquid)', NIGHT3 line 5; 'Off-distribution on purpose', base_cache.py docstring).

ARM A vs ARM B needs code that is not in the list of five changes. Today's specstep path is sequential: draft_chunk computes fast_x0 and then base_x0_at under DLOCK in the same thread. The measured run confirms this: 349 s = 284 s Base denoise + ~65 s Fast, with no overlap. Without a new Fast/Base thread, arm A at ctx 9 = 430 s vs arm B 375 s (0.87x). With the thread: 379 s vs 375 s (0.99x). For kv, Fast (1.4 s) is slower than Base (~0.9 s), so arm A is Fast-bound: 0.86-0.92x threaded, 0.67-0.71x sequential. The sequential kv case falls below the claimed 0.83 lower bound. In GPU-seconds, arm A uses 2 GPUs where arm B needs 1 (Fast is not needed in B), so efficiency is about 0.44-0.50x.

CEILING OVERSTATED: '1.33x with a perfect drafter and a spare Base GPU' is wrong. Getting 8 -> 6 sequential target calls per chunk requires evaluating z1, z2_draft and z3_draft at once, which takes 3 Base GPUs (batched forwards fail). The drafts also arrive only after Fast latency: commit 1.4 s + x0D 1.4 s + x0D 1.4 s. Modelled per chunk: with one spare Base GPU the ceiling is 1.02x (ctx 9) to 1.09x (ctx 0); with 3 Base GPUs it is 1.09x (ctx 9) to 1.22x (ctx 0), on 4 GPUs in total. That is below 0.4x in GPU-seconds. This correction strengthens the design's own conclusion that lookahead is not worth building.

COST MODEL: the 'linear, about 0.2 ms/token' claim is only approximately true. The measurements are 0.203 ms/token at 18.4k tokens and 0.233 ms/token at 32.3k. The fitted quadratic attention term gives about 0.29 ms/token at 60k tokens. That is why the ctx 0 cost rises to about 886 s.

MEMORY: T_PR uses only the low expert (t = 937.3 < 947; wan_i2v_A14B.py boundary = 0.947, verified). Peak is about 44 GB at ctx 9 and about 62 GB extrapolated at 39 latents: this fits. T_AR is at the edge. The measured specstep run with both experts resident at ctx 9 and CFG5 peaked at 78.7 GB on dev1 (peak_mem1_gb) out of 80 GB. T_AR at ctx 0 with both experts resident would OOM ('late chunks at 480p OOM with both', --resident help text), which forces 2 swaps per chunk at about 2-3 s each (28 GB H2D). Host RAM is fine: 755 GB total; non-resident mode pins 56 GB per process.

T_AR-kv IS NOT IMPLEMENTABLE AS STATED: KV = BaseKV(lambda: expert('low'), ...) hard-codes the low expert. Node 0 at t = 999.8 would therefore run the low expert outside its range, which is not the stated T_AR. A high-expert cache built from a clean t=0 prefix is known to break (rel err 1.1-1.9, NIGHT3 line 5). T_AR should be restricted to rp.

EXPERIMENT BUDGET: plausible only for T_PR rp ctx 9. Arms A+B are 32 runs at about 375-430 s each, i.e. 3.3-3.6 pair-hours of compute plus per-run model loading (UNVERIFIED, likely 1-3 min each). That is about 2-3 h wall-clock on two pairs, but only after tonight's qproto_a queue finishes. That queue still has about 8 Base-70 runs at ~2850 s each (arm D) plus the cr plans for 8 seeds x 2 prompts that T_PR needs. ctx 0 roughly doubles the A/B batch time to about 4.5-5 h. Adding T_AR adds about 2.5 h.

SMALLER FEASIBILITY RISKS (UNVERIFIED): (1) Chunk 0: torch.cat(outs, 1) raises on an empty list, and base_cond then needs F = 9. This is small. (2) The plan anchor is weak. At sigma 0.937 the plan carries 6.3% signal amplitude (SNR 0.0045), and Base never sees the plan hint (A4). NIGHT3 notes say Base's layout is 'not fixed until ~step 11 of 16' (sigma about 0.82), so the 1->2 renoise jump from x0_B(z1) may still snap back. (3) T_PR is 8-call chunk-wise RePaint, which is the always16 family whose seams persisted (NIGHT3 10:40 PM), so arm B may fail the drift/seam test. The exact sampler would then be exact for a bad target. (4) McNemar A-vs-B over 16 paired runs can only detect gross bugs. The in-run z-tests are the real exactness check.

(1) Replace 'Base-70 ~600 s' with the measured single-GPU 2766-3111 s (base70_s*/revisit.json). Report T_PR's advantage (about 441-508 s at ctx 9 including the plan) as a change of target, not a speculative gain, and give both wall-clock and GPU-seconds: arm A uses 2 GPUs, arm B uses 1. (2) Restate the lookahead ceiling as about 1.02-1.09x with one spare Base GPU (1.09-1.22x only with 3 Base GPUs and Fast latency included). (3) Add a sixth code change: run Fast x0/commit on dev0 in a thread alongside base_x0_at on dev1 (the run_early pattern). Otherwise arm A is about 0.87x at ctx 9, not about 0.99x. (4) Pin rp --ctx 9 for T_PR. Drop ctx 0 (about 950-1020 s, doubles the batch) and the kv target (known drift; kv_x0 hard-codes the low expert, so T_AR-kv is not the stated target). Run T_AR (rp, --resident, 78.7 GB measured peak at ctx 9) only after T_PR. (5) Update the alpha statement using tonight's per-position specstep log: alpha <= 10^-52.7 per chunk and <= 10^-18.2 per latent frame at the best chunk, still about 0. (6) Schedule arms A/B only after qproto_a has delivered all 16 Base-70 runs and the 16 cr plans, and budget about 2-3 h wall-clock on GPUs 4-7 for T_PR ctx 9 A+B.
